title: Senior Radar Integrator
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Radar Integrator to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The Senior Radar Integrator will support the Golden Dome for America (GDA) Sensors Capability Portfolio Manager (CPM) by providing integration and program management support across multiple complex sensors initiatives. This role is responsible for evaluating and coordinating the numerous components under CPM Sensors to ensure the programmatic and technical plans meet the GDA requirements and timelines.  The integrator will be tasked with substantial collaboration across the components to synchronize, define and document the key performance measures such as schedule drivers, integration activities, risks, and others. 
This position requires strong programmatic experience, technical prowess, and the ability to manage cross-functional workflows in a fast-paced environment. The Analyst will serve as a key integrator—translating technical and programmatic data into actionable plans and reports, ensure the GDA requirements and timelines are being met, and driving proactive execution across GDA’s engineering and programmatic portfolio.
Duties: 
Provide the business knowledge and technical skills to implement GDA strategies and plans
Coordinate GDA direction and alignment / flow-down to the individual GDA sensors program plans, requirements, including drafting, validating, and updating technical documentation (e.g., specifications, interface control documents, engineering change proposals).
Develop and maintain critical Knowledge Points / Technical Performance Measures for the underlayer radars that ensure alignment between technical activities, program milestones, and contractual deliverables.
Monitor contractor technical performance, reviewing monthly reports, validating engineering progress, and supporting technical assessments for contract actions.
Facilitate and support program / component reviews such as SRR, PDR, CDR, TIMs, and engineering working groups, ensuring action items, risks, and decisions are captured and tracked.
Support program planning artifacts, including Program Objective Memorandum (POM) inputs, acquisition documentation, and engineering resource forecasts.
Support the coordination, identification, development, tracking and mitigation of risks and issues, including technical, schedule, and integration risks
Participate in IPTs, PMRs, engineering boards, and cross-functional planning sessions, representing programmatic and technical integration interests.
Ensure compliance with DoD engineering, acquisition, and program management regulations, including DoD 5000 series, systems engineering policies, and relevant technical standards.
Assist in fiscal planning and execution by aligning component activities with budget profiles, spend plans, and funding constraints.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Minimum of 10 years of experience supporting Program management / Systems Engineering of complex DoW components is required with preferred experience support DoW ground based sensors 
Demonstrated experience supporting technical and financial execution 
Experience supporting requirements development / evaluation, developing roadmaps for software and hardware capabilities as well as developing integration strategies to deliver capabilities to warfighters.
Experience supporting program reviews evaluating technical review plans and objective evidence.
Demonstrated experience supporting contract development and negotiations ensuring the government desires are accurately coordinated with the prime
Experience with Technical Performance Measures (TPMs), and Knowledge Points (KPs)
Experience coordinating designs of subsytems and integration of total system. 
Familiarity with DoW acquisition processes, systems engineering lifecycle, and technical documentation standards.
Ability to interpret engineering data and translate it into programmatic impacts, risks, and decisions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex engineering and programmatic information to diverse audiences.
Ability to manage complex workloads and prioritize tasks without supervision.
Strong leadership, analytical, and organizational skills.
Must have a current driver’s license.
Travel: 10%
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
U.S. DoD Top Secret clearance is required.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s of Science required
Master’s degree preferred.
Desired Skills : 
Experience supporting DoW acquisitions and development of ground based radars
In-depth understanding of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process.
Ability to identify and implement innovative solutions to improve engineering and program management processes.

title: Program Integrator
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Program Integrator  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The Program Integrator supporting Advanced C-UAS Effects (ACE) Project Office ensures seamless integration across functional areas within the Product Office and synchronizes activities with supporting Project Management (PM) and Product Management (PdM) Offices, as well as external organizations. This role manages highly complex integration efforts spanning multiple technical disciplines, logistics concepts, and system‑of‑systems interfaces. The Program Integrator coordinates Government matrixed support and contractor teams to define interoperability requirements, align program tasks, and evaluate progress against program plans. The position supports senior leaders through analysis, planning, and decision‑quality products; facilitates cross‑organizational collaboration; identifies and mitigates programmatic and technical risks; and ensures effective implementation of program direction across all concurrent technical efforts.
Duties: 
Program Integration - Coordinate and integrate technical, programmatic, and logistics activities across PM ACE, supporting PM/PdM offices, and external organizations to ensure alignment with program objectives.
Stakeholder Coordination - Synchronize efforts across Government matrix support, contractor teams, and other Service partners to define interoperability requirements, validate interfaces, and maintain cohesive execution.
Systems & Interface Validation -Verify and validate system interfaces and integration points from technical, architectural, and logistics perspectives to support system‑of‑systems design.
Program Analysis & Risk Management - Collect and analyze program data to assess schedule and technical performance, identify risk areas, determine root causes of issues, and recommend corrective actions.
Tasking & Senior Leader Support - Manage taskings and deliverables; prepare senior‑level briefings, information papers, and reports; support IPTs and leadership engagements with decision‑quality products.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5+ years of relevant experience in Army, Joint, or DoD program/project management, integration, or operations.
Strong knowledge of DoD acquisition, program management, or systems integration processes.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate across diverse teams and stakeholders to achieve program goals.
Experience with task management tools, data visualization, or knowledge management platforms.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; experience developing and presenting senior-level briefings.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook).
Must have a current driver's license.
Travel: 10%
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field.
Master’s degree preferred.
Desired Skills : 
Experience supporting Army PM/PdM offices or acquisition organizations.
Background in systems engineering, interoperability, or logistics integration for complex defense programs.
Familiarity with Fires, C5ISR, or related mission areas.
Experience working in PEO Missiles & Space, RCCTO, or similar organizations.
Self‑starter with ability to operate independently while managing multiple priorities.

title: Program Acquisition Analyst & Advisor
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Program Acquisition Analyst & Advisor to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Program Acquisition Analyst and Advisor provides acquisition analysis, program management insight, and headquarters integration support to Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. The position requires an experienced Army acquisition professional who understands the Fires portfolio and can apply firsthand program management experience to assess program issues, develop recommendations, and support leadership decisions. The successful candidate will have progressive Army acquisition experience culminating in successful completion of a lieutenant colonel–level Centralized Selection List (CSL) acquisition Product Manager assignment. Direct acquisition experience within PEO Missiles and Space, the Rapid Capabilities and Critical Technologies Office (RCCTO), or PAE Fires is required. This is a hands-on analytical and coordination role. The individual develops decision materials, integrates program and staff inputs, tracks priority actions, and helps translate leadership direction into coordinated follow-through. 
Duties: 
Apply Army acquisition and Fires portfolio experience to analyze program execution, identify issues, and develop practical recommendations for leadership consideration.
Assess program cost, schedule, performance, and risk, identifying dependencies and decisions requiring headquarters attention.
Coordinate priority actions across program offices, portfolio elements, and functional staff; consolidate inputs and track actions through completion.
Prepare and refine briefings, decision papers, read-aheads, talking points, and executive correspondence that clearly explain issues, options, and recommended actions.
Support acquisition reviews, program reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites by coordinating materials, identifying decision requirements, and documenting outcomes.
Analyze the relationships among requirements, acquisition strategies, funding, contracting, testing, fielding, and sustainment to identify execution challenges and inform recommendations.
Support resource prioritization and Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) activities by assessing program needs, funding considerations, and portfolio impacts.
Coordinate with Army requirements organizations, acquisition stakeholders, and mission partners to clarify issues and support alignment across organizational boundaries.
Maintain visibility of leadership decisions, taskings, and commitments; identify delays or unresolved issues and coordinate follow-up.
Recommend improvements to acquisition processes, staff coordination, and portfolio governance based on practical program management experience.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
12 plus year of relevant DoD acquisition experience. 
Progressive experience in Army acquisition and program management, including assignments of increasing responsibility leading to CSL selection and service.
Direct acquisition experience within PEO Missiles and Space, RCCTO, or PAE Fires, with demonstrated knowledge of the Fires portfolio.
Substantive responsibility for acquisition program execution and demonstrated understanding of Fires programs, organizational relationships, capability priorities, and acquisition challenges.
Practical knowledge of the Army acquisition process and the Defense Acquisition System, including acquisition strategy development, milestone decisions, requirements integration, contracting, test and evaluation, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment.
Experience managing program cost, schedule, performance, and risk and presenting program status, issues, and recommendations to acquisition leadership.
Working knowledge of PPBE and the relationship between program execution, funding requirements, and resource decisions.
Demonstrated ability to develop clear briefings, decision papers, and written recommendations for senior leaders.
Ability to coordinate across program offices and functional staffs, reconcile competing inputs, and manage multiple actions with established deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
Ability to work onsite in Huntsville, Alabama, and travel approximately 10 percent. 
Must have a current driver's license. 
Must be a U.S. Citizen 
Must have an active U.S. DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have a Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this clearance level during their employment 
Education Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in engineering, business, management, public administration, or a related field.
Preferred / Desired Skills : 
Recent experience directly supporting or managing Army Fires acquisition programs.
Experience coordinating with acquisition headquarters and preparing materials for General Officer or Senior Executive Service reviews.
DAWIA Program Management certification at the Advanced level or equivalent prior certification.
Master’s degree in engineering, business, management, public administration, national security, military strategy, acquisition, or a related field.
Experience supporting portfolio reviews, cross-program integration, and resource prioritization.
Active Top Secret clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) eligibility.

title: Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking an Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a motivated recent Computer Science graduate to join our technical team as an Associate Data Integration & Software Specialist (Hybrid / On-Site). In this role, you will help design, build, and maintain data exchange pipelines and application interfaces that connect disparate internal databases and external partner platforms.
You will work closely with cross-functional engineering teams, product managers, and external stakeholders to ensure reliable, automated data flow across systems. This position offers an ideal bridge between core software engineering, data architecture, and technical project coordination.
Essential Job Functions 
Data Integration & Interface Development 
Design, build, and maintain data transformation routines and data exchange schemas (e.g., XML, JSON, REST APIs) to enable seamless communication between heterogeneous software platforms.
Implement parsers, validation routines, and automated import/export pipelines to ensure clean data migration and interoperability across systems.
Modernize legacy data structures and formats by converting them into standardized, scalable web and enterprise schema standards.
Conduct initial testing, debugging, and quality verification on data exchange workflows prior to deployment.
Technical Coordination & Project Support 
Coordinate cross-functional technical syncs and sprint reviews; assist in establishing sprint milestones and tracking team deliverables.
Document meeting notes, track action items, and follow up with internal development teams and external partners on technical requirements and open tickets.
Monitor project deadlines and proactively communicate roadblocks or timeline risks to technical leads and management.
Collaborate with senior engineers to evaluate potential vendor proposals, software tools, or third-party APIs for system compatibility and performance.
Documentation & Technical Communication 
Draft comprehensive system interface documentation, API specifications, data flow diagrams, and user guides.
Present technical updates, data metrics, and project status briefings to team leads, non-technical stakeholders, and peers.
Prepare clear technical write-ups proposing solutions or corrective actions for data pipeline bottlenecks.
General Team Responsibilities 
Collaborate with fellow developers, systems analysts, and operations personnel to support continuous integration and operational reliability.
Perform code reviews, adhere to standard version control practices, and follow team software development lifecycle (SDLC) standards.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
0-2 years of experience
Core Technical Knowledge: Strong foundational understanding of data structures, algorithms, relational/non-relational databases, and client-server architectures.
Data Interchange & Scripting: Hands-on experience (via coursework, academic projects, or internships) working with structured data formats (XML, JSON, CSV), schema validation (XSD, JSON Schema), and at least one programming/scripting language (e.g., Python, Java, C#, or JavaScript/Node.js).
Database Fundamentals: Proficiency with SQL and querying relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server).
Communication & Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to document code clearly and present technical concepts to peers and project leads.
Tools: Familiarity with modern collaboration suites (Microsoft Office 365, Teams, Slack) and version control platforms (Git/GitHub/GitLab).
Ability to travel up to 15–20% for on-site team planning or stakeholder workshops as required.
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Information Systems, or a closely related technical field (graduated within the last 12 months or nearing graduation).
Preferred: 
Exposure to RESTful API design, web services, or middleware/integration platforms.
Experience with ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines or messaging queues.
Prior internship, capstone project, or open-source contribution involving cross-system data transfer or interface design.
Basic understanding of project management methodologies (Agile/Scrum, Jira, Trello).

title: Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
PeopleTec is seeking a Systems Engineer/Analyst to support Missile Defense Agency Systems Engineering Directorate to provide Verification and Validation support for the System Verification Director . This position plays a key role in defining, analyzing, and managing requirements spanning the entire system life cycle - from concept development through testing and deployment.
Duties: 
Develop/maintain code for Ground Test and Flight Test data analysis required by MDA/SEQV. Coordinate with other developers collaborating on code modifications and analysis tools within a code repository of thousands of executable lines of python code housed in a git repository environment.
Write Python, MATLAB, and shell command scripts to verify and validate test system requirements for Missile Defense Elements using Ground Test and Flight Test data.
Execute System Interface Control Document (SICD) requirements checkout using MATLAB requirements analysis code against tactical message log data recorded from flight and ground test data sources.
Develop scripts to import, parse, and extract Missile Defense Data Center (MDDC) ground test and flight test data to be used for MDA/SEQV activities including Threat V&V analysis, Core Truth Model (CTM) analysis, SICD analysis, and System Federation Validation Events (SFVE) / System Post Flight Reconstruction (SPFR) performance parameter analysis.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5-8+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience in systems engineering supporting missile defense or other complex defense systems.
Must have a strong ability to use Python, MATLAB , and ability to execute operating system shell command scripts 
Strong understanding of MDA system architectures , lifecycle processes, and verification/validation. 
Ability to translate high-level mission objectives into detailed technical requirements.
Excellent analytical, documentation, and communication skills.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
An active DoD  Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active  Secret  clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.  
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and experience)

title: Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Mid-to-Senior-Level Engineer/Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
We are seeking a motivated engineer/analyst to provide Modeling and Simulation (M&S) Verification, Validation, and Accreditation (VV&A) support to the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) System Verification directorate. The selected candidate will serve a lead role for M&S accreditation efforts associated with Aegis BMD, Sensor (e.g., Cobra Dane, UEWR, AN/TPY-2, SBX, LRDR), or other models represented in the MDA Ground Test (GT) events. 
This is a full-time, on-site position at a government customer location. The selected candidate will collaborate with Government customers, internal and external Missile Defense Agency (MDA) stakeholders, program offices, and M&S development prime contractors.
Duties: 
Serve as subject matter expert for information (e.g., M&S versions, V&V plans, M&S versus tactical boundaries) associated with assigned Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) M&S.
Coordinate with model owners to develop executable action plans to ensure timely delivery of V&V evidence supporting accreditation information needs for MDA M&S accreditation assessments of applicable GT data sources.
Conduct technical review of V&V evidence and develop M&S accreditation recommendations for the MDA accreditation authority.
Author sections and/or provide technical input for relevant products such as the MDA M&S accreditation report/briefing, MDA M&S accreditation decision memorandum, and MDA M&S accreditation plan.
Develop Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M) to address high-priority issues affecting M&S accreditation.
Regularly interface with the model owner and V&V agent to address M&S limitations impacting accreditation outcomes. Document and maintain M&S limitation resolution plans in a dedicated online repository for tracking and reporting purposes.
Collaborate with model owners to maintain or refine Performance Parameters, Acceptability Criteria, and Evaluation Methodologies for inclusion in current and future releases of the M&S Accreditation Plan.
Support Operational Capability List (OCL) Working Group (OWG) meetings to brief MDA M&S accreditation status for HWIL models supporting Missile Defense System (MDS) performance assessment of capabilities to be fielded.
Provide regular verbal and written status updates to leadership regarding M&S VV&A areas of responsibility.
Perform other related tasks as assigned by the Director, MDA System Verification or M&S VV&A lead and strategic advisor.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5-8+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience with modeling and simulation applications.
Knowledge of M&S VV&A principles, methodologies, and accreditation processes.
Experience evaluating technical evidence of complex defense systems, and developing defensible engineering recommendations.
Familiarity with the Missile Defense System architecture and its integrated defense systems.
Ability to independently lead technical assessments, work within a multi-disciplinary team, develop action plans, and communicate status and findings to government leadership.
Strong technical writing, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
An active DoD  Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active  Secret  clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.  
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or related technical discipline.
Desired Skills : 
Top Secret clearance preferred.
Advanced degree in Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Demonstrated experience with the Aegis BMD weapon system and/or Sensor components of the Missile Defense System architecture.
Experience developing or reviewing M&S accreditation plans, V&V reports, accreditation assessments, and technical recommendations.

title: Senior Operations Research Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Operations Research Analyst  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
Duties: 
Candidate will serve as the Sr Operations Research Analyst to an Army Product Office responsible for the development and defense of cost estimates to support acquisition decision-making. 
Candidate will plan, coordinate, and conduct independent cost analysis for the assigned program ensuring technical appropriateness, soundness, and accurate interpretation of results with regard to cost and budget.
Perform the calculation and forecasting of the future costs of systems, projects/programs, resources, to support independent studies, funding decisions, and various management reviews (e.g., milestone reviews, budget reviews).
Create and maintain lifecycle cost estimates in ACE-IT. 
Develop cost estimating methodologies based on available data sources.  
Perform the planning and development of controls and provide expert technical analyses, budgetary advice, and guidance regarding the development and implementation of resource allocations and plans in order to defend budget activities. 
Conduct analysis and provide recommendations by applying expert knowledge of a broad range of cost analysis strategies to include mathematics, statistical analysis, parametric and non-parametric analysis, computer modeling, regression analysis, and economic analysis.
Coordinate with the PAE FIRES and PM IFMC Program Office Estimates for APBs and other milestone review documentation. 
Create documents and briefing charts that communicate current status and forecast on program with regard to cost. 
Receive and analyze Earned Value Management reports and make recommendations to Product Manager based on analysis. 
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
10-12 years of relevant work experience is desired.
History of supporting and engaging executive level leadership.
High understanding of MS Office suite and ACE-IT cost modeling experience is required. 
Knowledge of US Army acquisition processes and experience working and closing actions/taskers that are briefed to higher headquarters and executive leadership.  
The successful candidate will be highly organized, flexible and must demonstrate attention to detail and the ability to meet suspense’s.
Candidate must be able to work with minimum guidance in addressing actions, and then use their own knowledge, ingenuity, innovation and experience to complete the product.
Excellent written and verbal communication’s skills, people skills and enthusiasm are important, as well as the ability to handle a variety of tasks in a team environment. 
Candidate must be a resident of Huntsville, Alabama or be willing to relocate to the Huntsville, Alabama area.
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active Secret clearance upon hire, and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.
Education Requirements : 
A bachelors degree in mathematics, statistics, or Operations Research is desired.

title: Senior Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking an Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The candidate will serve as an Engineer within a Project Management Office (PMO) within PAE Fires and will be responsible for providing technical support to the program's Chief Engineer and the Product Manager. The candidate will provide network engineering expertise across the life cycle of tactical network capabilities integrated into Army Fires’ air defense weapon systems, spanning design, development, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment of network transport, data links, and secure information exchange. Work will emphasize LAN and WAN performance, secure information sharing across classification domains, cryptographic and communications security (COMSEC) integration, and technology refresh of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) network components driven by obsolescence and cybersecurity compliance. The candidate will prepare and present network findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. Will work within and/or lead a multidisciplinary team to achieve program goals. Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager. 
The candidate will interface with internal PMs across PAE Fires and external organizations to include HQDA, ASA(ALT), AvMC, ATEC, AMCOM, multiple Cross-Functional Teams, and others for coordination and synchronization of network technical and programmatic objectives. 
Duties: 
Provide network engineering support across the life cycle (design, development, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment) of tactical network capabilities integrated into PAE Fires air defense weapon systems. 
Plan and execute network and data link tests to assess and advance the capabilities of current and future operations across product office weapon systems. 
Analyze requirements documents, interpret technical and programmatic needs, and manage supplier network solutions for weapon system tactical networks and battlefield data dissemination across multiple networks. 
Provide technical expertise on networks and their components that integrate sensors, effectors, and fire control systems into a system of systems, including the configuration, installation, troubleshooting, and operation of the network topology. 
Support secure information exchange between networks operating at different classification levels, including cross-domain solution integration, security policy enforcement, and auditability. 
Oversee information classification and encryption or COMSEC requirements in support of Government solutions. 
Support technology refresh and obsolescence management of COTS network components to sustain compliant, supportable capability and maintain a viable authority to operate. 
Troubleshoot and sustain LAN and WAN operations, including simulated and test environments, and analyze real-world communication and performance issues. 
Develop and review technical documentation supporting installation, configuration, and troubleshooting of network equipment. 
Prepare and present network findings, reports, and improvement plans to management and stakeholders. 
Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager. 
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
10+ years of relevant network engineering experience. Additional education may be substituted for years of experience. 
Hands-on experience with LAN and WAN design, switching and routing, and network troubleshooting, particularly within defense environments. 
Experience with tactical network solutions, including their design, integration, and sustainment in support of weapon system operations. 
Working knowledge of network security, information assurance, and IAVA and RMF compliance. 
Familiarity with cryptographic and COMSEC devices and secure data transfer across classification domains. 
Strong knowledge of industry standards and defense requirements. 
Excellent communication and presentation skills. 
Ability to lead and work within a multidisciplinary team. 
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Secret clearance (with TS/SCI eligibility). 
Education Requirements: 
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline (for example, computer science or information technology); advanced degree preferred. 
Desired Experience: 
Previous experience working in or supporting a U.S. Government Program Office (preferred). 
Industry networking certifications such as CCNA or CCNP. 
Experience with cross-domain solutions, Army tactical networks and their components. 
Familiarity with Army acquisition processes and PAE Fires air defense programs.

title: AI/ML Lead (Speech, Model Tuning & Guardrails)
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking an AI/ML Lead (Speech, Model Tuning & Guardrails)  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
PeopleTec is seeking an AI/ML Lead in Huntsville, AL, to develop speech recognition, model-tuning, and safety capabilities for an on-premise AI system supporting the H-1 flight simulator. You will work with AI/ML, software, and aviation subject matter experts to adapt models to cockpit audio and military terminology, evaluate their performance, and ensure model outputs are safely handled before they can affect the simulator.

Strong Python skills and experience serving models on-premise using CUDA-capable hardware. 
Experience building and evaluating a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that produced reliable, expected results. 
Ability to travel occasionally for test events.

Experience integrating speech recognition and text-to-speech, including voice activity detection and audio pipelines for noisy environments. 
Experience with structured or schema-constrained generation, model-serving adapters, speech/audio pipelines, knowledge graphs or ontologies, and AI applications for aviation, training, or simulation. 
Experience with knowledge graphs and ontologies (OWL, RDF, SPARQL) and rule-based validation of generated structures. 
Experience in aviation, tactical training, or simulation, and working alongside an operator subject matter expert.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Systems Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Advanced Fires Project Office (AFPO) and Project Director Manager Scalable Hypersonics (PdM SHY) develop, integrate, and transition advanced weapon systems to meet critical Army operational needs. We are seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to serve as a technical leader guiding requirements, architecture, integration, risk management, and test activities across our rapidly expanding hypersonic portfolio.
The Senior Systems Engineer will manage a highly complex technical baseline, lead technical reviews, maintain strict configuration management, and advise government leadership on engineering risks and opportunities. Crucially, this role will deconflict overlapping technical efforts and resource demands across hypersonic programs (including MROM, ASHS, AHSS, Mach XL, Sirena, and PrsM Inc 4) to ensure responsible stewardship of USG resources.
Duties: 
Lead the development, validation, and maintenance of system requirements, system architecture, and rigorous traceability across the hypersonic portfolio.

title: Flight Test Engineer
text:

PeopleTec is currently seeking a Flight Test Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL location.

Ability to apply an interdisciplinary approach to ensure technical needs are translated into step-by-step processes to produce efficient and effective results

Familiar with high level programming languages such as C++, C#, and/or Python
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Project)
Familiarity with the development and integration of engineering tools into software
Sound oral communication and technical writing skills and the ability to clearly communicate technical approaches and findings to the team and the government customer
The ability and desire to work in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment

Bachelor’s degree in science or engineering or scientific field of study from an accredited college or university and 5 - 8+ years of progressively complex experience in modeling and simulation, software, aerospace systems, and/or flight testing

A relevant PhD degree in engineering or science from an accredited college or university may be substituted for three years of relevant work experience.

text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Contract Operations and Systems Specialist  to support our Huntsville, AL location.
The Contract Operations and Systems Specialist supports our Huntsville, AL location by providing contracting, procurement-policy, compliance, and operational support to a government contracting office. The position requires the skill set of an experienced Contract Specialist with an emphasis on preparing contractual and supporting acquisition documentation, maintaining file integrity and audit readiness, and supporting contracting-office administration. Working onsite as an integral member of the contracting team, the specialist researches and applies acquisition regulations and policy, drafts and reviews documentation for government approval, maintains electronic contract and agreement files, supports tasker and acquisition-system administration, and keeps the office's SharePoint content, trackers, permissions, and existing workflows current.
DUTIES: 
Draft, revise, and format contractual and supporting acquisition documentation for government review and approval, and research and apply applicable acquisition regulations, policy, and local procedures.
Review contractual and acquisition documentation for completeness, consistency, required approvals, and compliance with applicable policy and office procedures; identify deficiencies and track corrective actions to closure.
Create, organize, and maintain electronic contract and agreement files, including Other Transaction Agreement files when applicable, and support contract closeout, retention, and disposition requirements.
Conduct file health checks, maintain audit-readiness metrics, identify missing documentation, and support peer reviews, procurement management reviews, audits, and data calls.
Develop and maintain office templates, checklists, standard operating procedures, job aids, and policy or compliance guidance for government review and approval.
Maintain workload and suspense trackers; log, route, and track ETMS2 and other office taskers; prepare status information; and alert leadership to late or at-risk actions.
Provide administrative support for acquisition systems, user accounts, roles, recertifications, and access rosters; identify data discrepancies and route corrections to the responsible government official.
Maintain the office's SharePoint content, libraries, lists, metadata, permissions requests, trackers, and existing workflows, and provide basic user assistance on established processes.
Coordinate with contracting professionals, requiring activities, contracting officer's representatives, program analysts, leadership, and IT support personnel to obtain documentation, resolve administrative issues, and meet deadlines.
Provide administrative support for onboarding, departure processing, Defense Travel System actions, building and system access requests, and training records.
Handle controlled unclassified information and procurement-sensitive information in accordance with applicable security, privacy, and organizational conflict-of-interest requirements.
As workload allows, assist a warranted Contracting Officer or Ordering Official with preparing simple order actions, such as GSA Schedule and CHESS orders, including market research and price reasonableness documentation, and drafting the order for the warranted official's review and signature.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience: 
5-10 of progressively responsible experience in federal acquisition, contracting, procurement policy, contract compliance, or closely related contracting support, preferably in a Department of Defense environment.
Demonstrated experience preparing contractual and supporting acquisition documentation and applying federal acquisition regulations and policy.
Experience supporting contract-file organization, compliance reviews, audit readiness, procurement management reviews, or related quality-assurance activities.
Strong working knowledge of federal and Department of Defense contracting principles, terminology, documentation, and electronic contract-file requirements.
Exceptional written communication and document-development skills, with the ability to produce clear, accurate, and compliant contractual and administrative products.
Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through, and judgment when handling sensitive acquisition information and competing suspense dates.
Experience working independently in a deadline-driven contracting office and coordinating actions across multiple organizations and levels of leadership.
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, Adobe Acrobat, and SharePoint content maintenance.
Ability to maintain existing SharePoint libraries, lists, metadata, permissions requests, trackers, and workflows; advanced SharePoint development is not required.
Ability to learn and support government acquisition, task-management, and administrative systems and explain processes clearly to users.
Strong interpersonal and verbal communication skills and a professional, service-oriented approach when working with government personnel, supported organizations, industry, and contractor teammates.
Must have a current driver's license.
Travel: Up to 10%.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
Must have an active DoD Secret clearance upon hire and the ability to maintain it.

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in acquisition, contracting, business administration, finance, supply chain management, public administration, management, or a related field.

Prior experience as a Contract Specialist followed by work in procurement policy, compliance, quality assurance, or contracting-office operations.
Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act contracting certification, Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting, Defense Acquisition University coursework, or equivalent acquisition training.
Experience with Army Contract Writing System, Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment, ETMS2, Federal Procurement Data System, Electronic Document Access, Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System, and Army contracting-file requirements.

text:

The candidate will prepare and present exportability engineering findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. Architect conceptual export variants based on TSFD assessments, and evaluate these variants to ensure they meet required performance metrics while satisfying U.S. export security criteria. 
Use modeling and simulation to assess how proposed DEF modifications, such as altered guidance code or added AT hardware, will impact a system's baseline kinematic performance, weight, and operational lethality. 
Draft validated CPI and Critical Component Matrices and High-Level AT and Modularity Strategies, and support the technical drafting of formal foreign release documentation, such as Exception to the National Disclosure Policy (ENDP) Position Papers. 
Ensure compliance with defense and industry standards by managing exportability engineering processes effectively. 
Interface with internal teams and external organizations to coordinate exportability engineering objectives and strategies. 
Prepare and present exportability engineering findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. 
Conduct strategic planning and coordination to support program objectives. 
Provide technical guidance and leadership to peer and subordinate engineers within the exportability engineering team. 
Use digital tools and methodologies to manage cost, schedule, and performance for assigned activities. 
Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager. 
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
5+ years of relevant experience. Additional education may be substituted for years of experience. 
Demonstrated experience in exportability engineering, particularly within defense or aerospace industries. 
Working knowledge of Anti-Tamper (AT) principles, reverse engineering mitigation, and Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA). 
Experience with complex weapon systems, Counter-UAS (C-UAS) architectures, or advanced sensor/seeker integration. 
Proficiency with modeling and simulation tools used to assess kinematics and system performance impacts. 
Ability to translate complex TSFD and security requirements into actionable hardware and software engineering designs. 
Strong knowledge of industry standards and defense requirements. 
Excellent communication and presentation skills. 
Ability to lead and work within a multidisciplinary team. 
Previous experience working in a U.S. Government Program Office (required). 
Must be a U.S. Citizen. 
An active DoD clearance: Secret, with the ability to obtain TS/SCI.   
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

title: Special Programs Integration Engineer
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Special Programs Integration Engineer  to support our Huntsville, AL  location.
The Special Programs Integration Engineer serves as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Offensive Fires Command and Control (C2) Integration within the Product Manager Scalable Hypersonics (PdM SHY). Addressing a critical capability gap, this role provides technical leadership, C2 integration oversight, and systems engineering support across three active and expanding hypersonic missile programs. 
The primary focus is driving the near-term priority, Medium Range Offensive Munition (MROM) , by overseeing the complex integration of the Blackbeard hypersonic missile onto the HIMARS launch platform and subsequently onto the CAML launcher . The SME will spearhead intense coordination and technical collaboration across key external stakeholders, including PM STORM, the Software, Simulation, Systems Engineering and Integration (S3I) software development team, and PdM SHY leadership
DUTIES: 
Offensive Fires C2 Integration: Serve as the primary C2 Integration SME overseeing system architecture, software alignment, and tactical control capabilities across PdM SHY's hypersonic missile programs. 
MROM & Blackbeard Program Execution: Direct the technical integration of the Blackbeard hypersonic missile onto the HIMARS launch platform and manage follow-on integration efforts onto the CAML launcher in support of the MROM priority. 
Cross-Stakeholder Synchronization: Lead intense coordination and technical collaboration with PM STORM, the S3I software development team, PdM SHY, government matrix engineering teams, and industry partners. 
System-of-Systems Interface Alignment: Develop, refine, and validate interface requirements, Interface Control Documents (ICDs), and Concepts of Operation (CONOPS) for C2, missile, and launcher integration. 
Engineering Analysis & Technical Trade Studies: Conduct feasibility assessments, software/hardware trade studies, and integration evaluations to ensure seamless interoperability between launch platforms, C2 architectures, and strike weapon systems. 
Special Programs & Technical Oversight: Provide engineering support for sensitive, high-priority hypersonic and offensive fires initiatives within special access environments. 
Executive Decision Products: Prepare technical briefings, integration roadmaps, software interface specifications, and risk assessments for PdM SHY, PM STORM, and senior DoD leadership.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
7–10+ years of progressive engineering, technical project management, or system integration experience within DoD, U.S. Army, or Joint weapon system program offices. 
Offensive Fires & C2 Expertise: Demonstrated expertise in Command & Control (C2) systems integration, launch platform interfaces, or tactical fires software. 
System Engineering & Architecture: Strong background in systems engineering, requirements definition, software/hardware interface control (ICDs), and complex system-of-systems integration. 
Multi-Agency Stakeholder Coordination: Proven ability to drive consensus and lead complex integration efforts across external PMs, software centers (e.g., S3I), and cross-functional government teams. 
Communication: Exceptional oral and written communication skills with experience presenting technical decision products to senior Army and DoD leadership. 
Tools: Proficiency with standard Microsoft Office products (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Project). 
Must possess a valid driver's license
Travel: 10%
Must be a U.S. Citizen
An active DoD Top Secret clearance is required to perform this work. Candidates are required to have an active DoD Top Secret / SCI with Special Access Required (TS/SCI/SAR) upon hire , and the ability to maintain this level of clearance during their employment.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Aerospace, Systems, Electrical, Mechanical, Software) or a closely related technical field. 
Master’s degree preferred.

Experience working within PEO Missiles and Space, RCCTO, DARPA, or Service Research Laboratories.

title: Business and Financial Analyst
text:
Opportunity
PeopleTec is currently seeking a Business and Financial Analyst to support our Huntsville, AL location.
We are seeking a Business and Financial Analyst to support the Army’s Portfolio Acquisition Executive Fires Office (PAE Fires). This role involves leading budget formulation, execution, and reporting activities to ensure the effective allocation and utilization of resources in support of mission objectives. The Budget Analyst will collaborate with program managers, contracting officers, and other stakeholders to ensure compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) financial regulations and policies. This is a fast-paced role requiring strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
Duties: 
Develop, prepare, and manage program budgets, including Program Objective Memorandum (POM) submissions, spend plans, and obligation/expenditure forecasts.
Coordinate and execute funding actions, including drafting and submitting Purchase Requisitions (PRs), Military Interdepartmental Purchase Requests (MIPRs), and Direct Charge (DC) transactions.
Monitor and track the execution of funds to ensure alignment with program goals and timelines.
Conduct detailed financial analyses to identify trends, variances, and risks.
Prepare and present financial reports, briefings, and recommendations to leadership and stakeholders.
Maintain historical financial records and update funding history tracking when funds are received.
Monitor contract status, including ceiling limits, periods of performance, and funding requirements.
Support Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs) by analyzing monthly contractor reports, facilitating communication, and supporting  documentation for contract actions (e.g. Technical Directives (TDs) and Requests for Services Contract Approval (RSCAs).
Participate in Contract Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Program Management Reviews (PMRs), and financial/metrics meetings.
Ensure compliance with DoD financial management regulations, policies, and procedures.
Facilitate fiscal year-end close to ensure 100% obligation of expiring funds.
Support audits and reviews by providing accurate and timely financial data.
Coordinate with program managers and technical leads to align financial plans with program objectives.
Facilitate financial communication and coordination between the Project Office, higher headquarters, and external customers.
Qualifications
Required Skills/Experience : 
Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in budget analysis, financial management, or related roles, preferably within the DoD or federal government.
Demonstrated experience with DoD financial systems, including General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS).
Experience preparing and submitting PRs, MIPRs, and DC transactions.
Proven ability to monitor funds execution and create financial reports.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including advanced Excel functions (e.g., pivot tables, VLOOKUP, and data visualization).
Familiarity with financial management tools and software used in DoD environments.
Strong understanding of DoD financial regulations, including the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and DoD Financial Management Regulation (FMR).
Knowledge of appropriations, funding types, and fiscal law principles.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial data to diverse audiences.
Ability to manage diverse workloads of complex and priority projects without supervision.
Strong leadership, analytical, and organizational skills.
Must have a current driver's license. 
Travel: 20% 
Must be a U.S. Citizen 
Active U.S. DoD Secret clearance is required to perform this work. 
Education Requirements : 
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
Master’s degree preferred.
Desired Skills : 
10+ years of relevant experience in financial management, budget analysis, or related roles within the DoD.
Certification in financial management or related areas (e.g., Certified Defense Financial Manager (CDFM), DoD Financial Management Certification).
Familiarity with rapid acquisition or prototyping programs and their unique financial requirements.
In-depth understanding of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process.
Ability to provide guidance and informal mentoring to junior analysts, as required.
Ability to identify and implement innovative solutions to improve financial processes and program outcomes.
Experience using data visualization and advanced analytics tools.

The position will provide leadership across complex in vitro and computational approaches, including organ-on-a-chip (OOC) platforms, organoids, microphysiological systems, advanced tissue models, biological assays, and integrated experimental–computational systems. The Branch Lead will foster collaboration across experimental biology, bioengineering, computational modeling, data science, and software engineering to develop predictive, human-relevant technologies. This individual will serve as a senior technical representative for CFD Research, working with government sponsors, industry partners, and academic collaborators to understand emerging needs and translate them into innovative research programs and technology solutions. The Branch Lead will also play a key role in strategic growth, proposal development, customer engagement, talent development, and technology transition. The ideal candidate is an established scientific leader who combines expertise in complex biological systems and NAMs with a demonstrated ability to build teams, integrate multidisciplinary capabilities, lead complex R&D programs, develop new technologies, cultivate external partnerships, and translate scientific innovation into mission-relevant solutions.

Branch Leadership & Development

About the Job
CFD Research is excited to invite applications for a full-time Maintainability and Testability Engineer! In this role, you'll play a key part in supporting the continued growth, production, and lifecycle management of a complex multidisciplinary aerospace and defense hardware system.
Your mission will be to develop and enhance the engineering framework that ensures our system can effectively detect and isolate failures, support troubleshooting, provide vital diagnostic information, facilitate efficient maintenance, and be ready for service after maintenance activities.
You’ll have the opportunity to collaborate closely with a diverse team, including reliability experts, systems engineers, design engineers, controls and software professionals, test engineers, manufacturing teams, product support staff, maintainers, technicians, and program leaders.
Travel to our Test Facility in Hollywood, AL will be required once every two weeks.
About the Role
As the Maintainability and Testability Engineer, you’ll evaluate the system from the perspective of the personnel who maintain and support it throughout its lifecycle. Your insights will translate known and predicted system failure behaviors into practical requirements and strategies for fault detection, fault isolation, built-in testing, diagnostics, accessibility, maintenance, repair, support equipment, and verification.
This position offers significant involvement in design maturation, where you’ll leverage information from FMEA and FMECA, testing, maintenance activities, and real-world failure experiences to identify opportunities for enhancing system maintainability and testability.
What You’ll Do
Develop and maintain the system maintainability and testability engineering framework.
Develop and maintain Maintenance Task Analyses.
Perform or support Level of Repair Analysis.
Develop fault detection and fault isolation analyses.
Define expected fault-isolation capability and diagnostic resolution.
Develop and maintain integrated diagnostics and testability analyses.
Evaluate Built-In-Test capabilities, diagnostic coverage, limitations, and failure-detection performance.
Collaborate with controls, software, electrical, mechanical, and other engineering teams to enhance BIT and diagnostic functionality.
Assess health-monitoring and prognostic capabilities where applicable.
Work alongside the Systems Reliability Engineer to ensure significant failure modes identified through FMEA and FMECA are appropriately detectable and isolatable.
Evaluate accessibility, removal and replacement activities, maintenance sequences, maintenance times, tooling, personnel requirements, and support-equipment needs.
Identify maintainability-related design deficiencies and collaborate with responsible design organizations to develop corrective actions.
Support Reliability Centered Maintenance activities and the development of maintenance tasks and intervals.
Assist in repair-versus-replace decisions and other repair-level analyses.
Develop the engineering basis for maintenance and repair procedures and support the development of technical publications.
Review maintenance manuals, troubleshooting procedures, and related technical content for consistency with the system design and diagnostic strategy.
Identify and evaluate support-equipment requirements associated with system maintenance, troubleshooting, and diagnostics.
Support Human Systems Integration activities affecting system operation and maintenance.
Develop or support maintainability, BIT, diagnostics, fault-isolation, and human-engineering demonstrations.
Define verification approaches and evidence required to demonstrate compliance with maintainability and testability requirements.
Collaborate with the Systems Test Engineer to develop and execute formal maintainability, BIT, diagnostics, and fault-isolation verification activities.
Evaluate actual maintenance, test, and failure data to refine maintainability assumptions and diagnostic strategies.
Support product-support and lifecycle engineering activities requiring maintainability or testability expertise.
Basic Qualifications: 
Bachelor’s degree in systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, industrial engineering, or another closely related engineering discipline.
Three or more years of relevant engineering experience involving maintainability, testability, diagnostics, maintenance engineering, product support, hardware integration, testing, or a related technical area.
Understanding of hardware failure modes and the relationship between failure behavior, fault detection, fault isolation, troubleshooting, and repair.
Ability to understand technical drawings, system architecture, controls logic, maintenance information, test results, and engineering requirements.
Strong technical writing and analytical skills.
Ability to work directly with engineers, technicians, maintainers, test personnel, and product-support personnel.
U.S. citizenship required due to the nature of the company's work and contractual requirements.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance, as required.
Desired Qualifications: 
Experience developing Maintenance Task Analyses, Level of Repair Analysis, Reliability Centered Maintenance, or related maintenance engineering products.
Experience with Built-In-Test, integrated diagnostics, fault detection, fault isolation, or testability analysis.
Experience with FMEA or FMECA and translating failure modes into diagnostic or maintenance requirements.
Experience developing or evaluating maintainability demonstrations.
Experience working directly with maintainers or technicians on complex aerospace, defense, industrial, or electromechanical hardware.
Experience with technical publications, troubleshooting procedures, support equipment, or product-support analysis.
Experience supporting DoD acquisition, qualification, production, or lifecycle sustainment programs.
Experience with Cameo Systems Modeler, SysML, or other MBSE tools is beneficial.

Job Description: 
The Rotorcraft Flight Dynamics Modeling and Simulation Engineer will support Army rotorcraft engineering efforts through the development, improvement, and application of flight-dynamics models for both legacy fleet and future vertical lift, including models needed for real-time piloted simulations.  Additionally, the position will support the development of flight-dynamics models for simulation of advanced and novel vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft configurations, both manned and unmanned.
Advanced flight-dynamics modeling and analysis tools such as Gen Hel, FORECAST, and HeliUM are used to predict the responses of Army rotorcraft under various configurations and flight conditions, including real-time simulation with a pilot in the loop. They are also used to generate high-order linear models that are needed to design and optimize both flight controls and autonomy algorithms for Army rotorcraft.
Responsibilities 
Develop effective working relationships and collaborate with Army engineers and managers
Perform flight dynamics modeling and simulation of modern vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft configurations, both manned and unmanned.
Provide flight dynamics modeling expertise to the Future Long Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA) program office.  Participate in FLRAA design reviews and keep abreast of flight dynamics modeling needs for the FLRAA aircraft.  Develop, update, validate both generic and specific physics-based models of the FLRAA tiltrotor.
Develop proficiency with the HeliUM comprehensive modeling tool.  Update HeliUM as need to generate reduced-order real-time aerodynamics simulation models for UAS.
Develop and validate UH-60M flight dynamics simulation models to enhance existing capabilities by enabling the modeling and simulation of relevant rotorcraft configurations.  Assess and plan the necessary source code modifications and investigate considerations for the software development environment.
Conduct applied research to develop and validate advanced identification techniques needed to accurately model configurations with multiple redundant effectors.  Validate and update models so that they can in-turn be used to more accurately predict further configuration changes.
Attend technical group meetings, branch meetings, design reviews, etc. and report project updates and activities.
Communicate research results through technical presentations and written reports.

CFD Research is seeking a Senior Software Developer to lead efforts within a multidisciplinary team building cutting-edge tools to analyze, reduce, and visualize complex simulation data for missile defense systems. This role focuses on driving Post-Test Analysis (PTA) architecture, leading trade studies, architecting automated test frameworks, and guiding Agile software delivery. Partnering with customer software development leadership, you will architect solutions to accelerate test-case generation, ensure data validation accuracy for formal test events, and optimize system resource utilization across complex software suites.
Key Responsibilities 
Lead trade studies to evaluate and select potential PTA tools, presenting strategic recommendations to senior leadership; define Concept of Operations (CONOPs), test procedures, and message/data validation standards.
Drive feature backlog prioritization and architecture in Jira alongside the GSD team; design, implement, and review complex PTA codebases to automate end-to-end test-step validation.
Architect automated input generation frameworks to dramatically boost the speed, scale, and efficiency of building complex test cases.
Spearhead technical progress demos of working test scripts, establish code quality and peer review standards, and author user guides and documentation on analysis best practices.
Basic Qualifications 
U.S. Citizenship required; must possess and maintain an active DoD SECRET Clearance 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Math/Statistics, Physics, or a related STEM discipline with 8+ years of software engineering experience
Advanced programming skills in Python, MATLAB, and C++ with a proven track record of designing extensible, multi-language software architectures
Deep experience in object-oriented design patterns, software architecture, and system design
Proficiency with enterprise version control systems, CI/CD workflows, and Git repository management
Proven ability to lead technical trade studies, present complex architectural recommendations to executive stakeholders, and mentor team members through technical demos and reviews
Preferred Qualifications 
Extensive experience leading Agile software teams (Jira) and architecting enterprise software tools for data validation, script automation, or requirements verification
Domain experience with missile defense simulation/test architectures
Hands-on expertise architecting containerized environments (Docker) and embedding Test-Driven Development (TDD) methodologies across teams
Mastery of Python data science stacks (pandas, scipy, scikit-learn) and interactive visualization frameworks (Matplotlib, Plotly, Dash) for high-dimensional data reduction, modeling, and automated reporting
Location:   This role is based in the Huntsville, AL area ,  and is 100% onsite. 
Benefits: CFD Research offers competitive salaries and excellent employee benefits, including an employer matching 401(k) and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP). CFD Research offers our Full-Time, permanent employee-owners a highly competitive insurance package, including medical, vision, and dental insurance. Additionally, we offer company paid leave, compensation time, parental leave, long-term and short-term disability, accidental death and dismemberment, and life insurance. CFD Research Corporation is adding a talented transient dynamic finite element engineer to our growing structural analysis team. The candidate will evaluate high speed dynamic damage events in the time domain such as drops and bird strikes in aid of the design, verification and manufacture of aerospace structures. Experience with turbomachinery and rotordynamics is a plus.
The position is located at CFD Research’s Huntsville Headquarters, where the candidate will work closely with existing structural, fluid and thermal analysis teams to provide rapid design recommendations and assessments. The candidate is expected to interface regularly with Prototype, Test and Evaluation Division engineers located at the company’s Hollywood, AL Engineering Test Center. - Experience with rotordynamics and associated analysis methods

About the Job
CFD Research is seeking a full-time Systems Reliability Engineer to support the continued maturation, verification, and production of a complex multidisciplinary aerospace and defense hardware system.
The Systems Reliability Engineer will maintain and mature the program reliability engineering framework and will work closely with design engineering, systems engineering, test, manufacturing, quality, maintainability and testability, product support, and program leadership.
The position will be responsible for maintaining the quantitative reliability prediction model in Windchill as well as developing and maintaining FMEA and FMECA, reliability allocations, failure analyses, reliability fault trees, FRACAS analytics, reliability-growth assessments, and critical-item evaluations.
Travel to our Testing Facility in Hollywood, AL will be required x2/week.
About the Role
The Systems Reliability Engineer will be responsible for understanding how the system can fail, how often failures are expected to occur, which failure modes dominate system reliability, and whether design and corrective actions are improving the system as intended.
The reliability prediction model, FMEA and FMECA, failure analyses, and FRACAS information will be maintained as living engineering products and updated as the system design changes, component selections mature, verification testing generates new information, failures occur, and corrective actions are implemented.
The engineer will also provide reliability inputs to the assigned System Safety owner, including relevant failure modes, failure rates, fault logic, criticality information, and corrective-action status when those inputs are needed to maintain system hazard analyses or safety assessments.
What You’ll Do
Develop, maintain, and mature the system reliability prediction model using Windchill.
Maintain consistency between the reliability prediction model, current system configuration, component and assembly information, and applicable reliability assumptions.
Update reliability predictions as designs mature, parts change, operating assumptions change, failure data become available, or corrective actions modify the system configuration.
Develop and maintain reliability allocations and predictions at appropriate system, subsystem, assembly, and component levels.
Evaluate predicted reliability against system requirements and identify significant reliability drivers, contributors, and areas of insufficient margin.
Work with design engineering and other technical organizations to obtain component data, operating conditions, duty cycles, environmental assumptions, and failure information required to maintain the reliability model.
Develop, maintain, and mature system-level FMEA and FMECA analyses.
Coordinate subsystem and component failure-mode information with responsible engineering organizations.
Maintain failure severity, criticality, consequence, and related analytical information as the design and operating knowledge mature.
Develop and maintain reliability fault-tree analyses where appropriate.
Analyze test, manufacturing, and operational failure information for trends, recurring failure mechanisms, and emerging reliability risks.
Support and maintain the technical analysis portion of the program FRACAS process.
Work with responsible engineering organizations to investigate failures, identify root causes, establish corrective actions, and evaluate corrective-action effectiveness.
Use actual test, manufacturing, and operational failure information to assess and refine reliability-model assumptions where appropriate.
Evaluate the reliability impact of engineering changes and proposed corrective actions.
Maintain traceability between reliability predictions, FMEA and FMECA results, critical-item assessments, FRACAS information, and the current technical baseline.
Identify reliability-critical items using applicable failure analyses, reliability predictions, design information, operational information, and program criteria.
Generate reliability-model results and supporting analyses for technical reviews, customer deliverables, design trades, and verification activities.
Work with the Maintainability and Testability Engineer to ensure significant failure modes are appropriately detectable, isolatable, and maintainable.
Work with the Verification, Compliance and MBSE Systems Engineer to identify and trace verification evidence needed to support reliability requirements and analytical conclusions.
Provide reliability data and analyses to the assigned System Safety owner where reliability information supports hazard analysis, safety assessment, or safety-critical item decisions.
Basic Qualifications: 
Bachelor’s degree in reliability engineering, systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, chemical engineering, or another relevant technical discipline.
Three or more years of experience involving reliability engineering, failure analysis, hardware development, or a closely related engineering activity.
Experience developing, maintaining, or interpreting quantitative reliability prediction models for complex hardware systems.
Experience developing, maintaining, or using FMEA, FMECA, fault-tree analysis, or similar reliability engineering products.
Ability to work with component-level reliability information, system configurations, operating environments, duty cycles, failure-rate data, and engineering assumptions to maintain a defensible system reliability prediction.
Ability to understand multidisciplinary hardware systems and evaluate failure propagation and consequence.
Experience investigating technical failures and working with design engineers to establish root cause and corrective action.
Strong technical writing and analytical communication skills.
Ability to translate analytical findings into practical engineering actions and verification needs.
U.S. citizenship required due to the nature of the company's work and contractual requirements.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance, as required.

Experience using Windchill for reliability prediction, reliability analysis, or related reliability and maintainability activities.
Experience maintaining reliability models through design maturation, configuration changes, testing, production, and corrective-action implementation.
Experience correlating predicted reliability with actual failure information obtained through FRACAS, testing, manufacturing, or operational use.

text:

Magazine's Inc5000 as a top growing company for four of the last five years. Learn more at  www.cfd-research.com 
About the Job
CFD Research is seeking a full-time Systems Test Engineer to support the continued development, verification, and qualification of a complex multidisciplinary aerospace and defense hardware system.
The Systems Test Engineer will serve as a primary technical integrator for formal system verification testing and will work closely with systems engineering, mechanical and electrical engineering, controls, software, modeling and simulation, manufacturing, quality, reliability, maintainability, test operations, external test facilities, and program leadership.
The position will support a mature requirements-based verification program with a large number of requirements verified through formal testing. The Systems Test Engineer will organize those requirements into efficient test activities, develop and integrate formal test documentation, coordinate test readiness and execution, and ensure that test results provide objective evidence supporting system verification.
Travel to our test facility in Hollywood, AL x2/week is required.
About the Role
The Systems Test Engineer will be responsible for planning and integrating the system verification test program from verification planning through final test reporting.
The role requires strong technical breadth and the ability to translate system requirements into executable test activities while coordinating the specialized knowledge of multiple engineering disciplines. The engineer is not expected to independently replace the technical expertise of the organizations responsible for the systems being tested. Detailed technical content will be developed collaboratively with the applicable subject matter experts.
The engineer will work closely with the Verification, Compliance and MBSE Systems Engineer and Lead Systems Engineer to maintain traceability between system requirements, test activities, test configuration, test evidence, and final verification status.
What You’ll Do
Develop and maintain the integrated system verification test strategy and associated test planning.
Organize requirements assigned to verification by test into logical and efficient test events to minimize unnecessary duplication of testing.
Develop formal verification test plans identifying test objectives, applicable requirements, system configuration, operating conditions, resources, instrumentation, required evidence, and acceptance criteria.
Develop and integrate formal test procedures using technical content provided by applicable engineering subject matter experts.
Review internally and externally generated test procedures to confirm that planned testing adequately addresses assigned verification requirements.
Coordinate internal and offsite verification testing with engineering teams, test organizations, customer or government facilities, and external test providers.
Work with engineering subject matter experts to define required operating conditions, measurements, ranges, accuracy, sampling, instrumentation, and technical acceptance criteria.
Coordinate with controls, instrumentation, data acquisition, and test personnel to ensure required measurements and test capabilities are available.
Conduct or support formal test readiness reviews and verify that required procedures, configurations, instrumentation, personnel, facilities, and technical approvals are in place before testing begins.
Maintain test configuration control and ensure test evidence can be traced to the specific hardware, software, firmware, and system configuration evaluated.
Coordinate formal test execution and maintain visibility of deviations, anomalies, incomplete objectives, and test failures.
Initiate or support failure reporting and corrective action activities associated with verification test failures.
