In this role, supporting the Targets and Countermeasures team of the Missile Defense Agency (MDA, you will be directly responsible for verifying that critical missile flight hardware and propulsion systems are designed, fabricated, integrated, and tested strictly in accordance with baseline standards. You will evaluate prime contractor design and manufacturing processes, conduct technical reviews, and enforce compliance with industry mission assurance frameworks—specifically AIAA S-113 (Criteria for Explosive Systems and Devices on Space and Launch Vehicles) and related aerospace standards (such as AIAA S-114, AIAA S-080/081, SMC-S-016, or AFSPCMAN 91-710).
What You'll Be Doing : 
Design & Build Verification: Audit prime contractor engineering designs, drawing packages, manufacturing processes, and assembly records to ensure end items are built strictly to approved baseline specifications and flight-worthiness requirements.
AIAA S-113 & Standards Compliance: Apply AIAA S-113 (and related space/launch vehicle standards) to assess ordnance, explosive devices, pyrotechnic separation mechanisms, pressure vessels, and mechanical/propulsion subsystems across all design and production phases.
Peer Reviews & Milestone Gates: Participate in technical baseline reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, MRR, FRR), ensuring objective evidence supports mission assurance criteria before moving to integration and flight test.
Nonconformance & Root Cause Analysis: Evaluate Material Review Board (MRB) dispositions, deviations, and waivers. Oversee Failure Review Boards (FRBs) to determine root cause and ensure proper corrective/preventative actions (CAPA) are implemented.
Hardware Acceptance & Verification: Review and approve Qualification and Acceptance Test Procedures (QTPs/ATPs) and corresponding test results. Serve as the on-site engineering witness during critical testing events as required.
Supplier Integration & Oversight: Lead Integrated Product Team (IPT) meetings with supplier partners to maintain rigorous schedule alignment, track deliverables, and drive rapid technical problem resolution . 
What Required Skills You'll Bring : 
Active DoD Secret 
Bachelor's Degree, with additional years able to count in lieu of a degree in Engineering or an equivalent technical/scientific discipline degree related to area of specialty and
5+ years of experience, with additional education and certifications able to count in lieu of a degree
Demonstrated working knowledge and practical application of AIAA S-113 (or closely related launch/flight vehicle criteria such as AIAA S-114, SMC-S-016, TOR standards, or NASA-STD-8739/AFSPCMAN equivalents).
Proven ability to interpret technical drawings, schematics, engineering change orders (ECOs/ECPs), and manufacturing work instructions to verify build integrity.
Strong technical writing and presentation skills, capable of defending engineering assessments to government program leadership and contractor teams. 
What Desired Skills You Might Bring : 
Bachelor of Science in STEM Field with 7+ years supporting missile defense or large-scale, complex DoD programs. Strong preference for Aerospace, Mechanical, and Electrical engineering.

title: Cloud Platform Architect
text:
The Cloud Platform Architect defines the target-state technical architecture and long-term platform strategy for secure, resilient, scalable hybrid and multi-cloud mission environments. This role establishes architectural direction, governance, technical standards, and reference patterns for enterprise cloud modernization while remaining hands-on in prototyping, validating, automating, and troubleshooting platform capabilities.
Define target-state architectures for hybrid and multi-cloud platforms supporting Department of War (DoW) mission requirements.
Establish enterprise and program-level architecture principles, technology standards, reference architectures, reusable design patterns, and configuration baselines.
Develop strategies for integrating on-premises data centers with Azure, AWS, and other authorized cloud environments.
Design, prototype, and validate platform architectures covering compute, storage, networking, identity, security, data, containers, observability, automation, backup, disaster recovery, and continuity of operations.
Build and maintain proof-of-concept, prototype, and reference platform environments to validate architectural designs, technology selections, security controls, and integration patterns.
Develop, review, and troubleshoot infrastructure-as-code using Terraform, Bicep, AWS CloudFormation, Ansible, or comparable automation frameworks.
Design, deploy, configure, and troubleshoot cloud and hybrid-networking components, including virtual networks, subnets, routing, network-security controls, firewalls, load balancers, private connectivity, virtual private networks, and Domain Name System services.

Deploy, configure, secure, and troubleshoot container platforms and supporting services, including Kubernetes clusters, container registries, ingress, workload identity, and cluster security controls.
Develop and validate DevSecOps pipelines that incorporate source control, automated testing, artifact management, infrastructure deployment, container scanning, security checks, and configuration-compliance capabilities.
Configure and tune observability capabilities, including centralized logging, metrics, alerting, tracing, dashboards, service-health monitoring, and incident-response integrations.
Conduct hands-on performance, resiliency, backup, recovery, failover, and disaster-recovery testing; document results, identify gaps, and recommend remediation.
Analyze cloud configurations, logs, network flows, security findings, and operational telemetry to diagnose complex infrastructure and application-platform issues.
Ensure architecture decisions and technical implementations align with mission objectives, cybersecurity requirements, Zero Trust principles, resiliency goals, and operational constraints.
Evaluate emerging cloud and platform technologies through technical research, prototypes, and testing, and determine their applicability to the mission environment.
Lead architecture reviews and adjudicate technical tradeoffs among performance, security, cost, interoperability, portability, and maintainability.
Define migration and modernization strategies for legacy infrastructure and applications, including sequencing, transition architectures, implementation dependencies, and rollback considerations.
Establish architecture-governance processes, technical decision records, exception processes, configuration standards, implementation documentation, build guides, and operational runbooks.
Participate in technical working sessions, code and infrastructure-as-code reviews, design reviews, and operational-readiness reviews; provide practical engineering feedback based on implementation results.
Collaborate directly with cloud engineers, cybersecurity personnel, network engineers, application teams, and operations staff to resolve implementation issues and transition architectures into operational use.
Provide senior technical leadership and briefings to government executives, program managers, engineering leadership, and mission stakeholders.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related discipline; equivalent experience may be considered.
12+ years of progressively responsible infrastructure and cloud engineering experience, solutions engineering, systems engineering, or technical architecture.
Deep expertise in hybrid and multi-cloud architecture, preferably spanning Azure and AWS.

title: Technical Writer
text:
At i3, we value creativity, collaboration, and a relentless commitment to delivering quality products to our nation’s warfighters. We are searching for a talented, motivated, and driven Technical Writer to join our team. If you have a passion for clear communication and want to help shape the future of defense mission integration, we want to hear from you!
The successful candidate will directly support the Theater Operational Planning-Toolkit (TOP-T), a critical Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) mission integration and planning tool. Fielded in multiple theaters and utilized in real-world operations, TOP-T mitigates Anti-Access/Area Denial (A2/AD) challenges and supports Sensor-to-Shooter architectures.
This is a dual-impact role where you will not only be our go-to expert for technical documentation but also a key contributor to our software testing efforts. You will directly support the Theater Operational Planning-Toolkit (TOP-T), a critical Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) mission integration and planning tool. Fielded in multiple theaters, TOP-T is used in real-world operations to mitigate Anti-Access/Area Denial (A2/AD) challenges and support Sensor-to-Shooter architectures.
As a core member of our on-site IVV&E team at Redstone Arsenal, AL, you will play a vital part in ensuring the quality and usability of this critical system.
Duties of the tech writer position include, but are not limited to, the following:
Develop, write, and edit a variety of technical documents, including training manuals, user guides, reports, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Ensure all documentation meets military standards for style, format, and quality.
Collaborate with engineers, software developers, and business partners to translate complex technical information into clear, concise content.
Design and incorporate graphics, illustrations, and presentations to enhance technical materials.
Participate in software testing activities as an integral member of the IVV&E team.
Contribute to project deliverables and track performance metrics.
A bachelor’s degree and at least 1 year of experience in technical writing or developing training materials.
An active DoD security clearance, with the ability to maintain it.

text:

JOB SUMMARY 
We are seeking a Senior DevSecOps Engineer to operate the cloud infrastructure our engineering teams depend on today and to build its successor from the ground up. The current environment spans AWS, Kubernetes, and CI. The next one is a new AWS GovCloud organization defined entirely as code, with the networking, identity, and software supply chain that a regulated engineering organization needs. 
You will keep the existing environment healthy while the new one takes shape, then move workloads into it. You will also run the tooling that gives our engineers governed access to AI models and coding agents. 
This is a building role on a small team, and the scope is broad by design. You will not maintain a compliance binder; you will turn security requirements into code that produces its own evidence. 
Key Responsibilities 
Operate and improve our existing AWS environments, Kubernetes clusters, and CI platform, and migrate workloads into the new organization as it comes online
Build a new multi-account AWS GovCloud organization as code
Build and operate segmented network planes: Transit Gateway, Firewalls, IPAM, PrivateLink, and VPNs to our facilities
Deliver secure environment ingress / egress
Own the software supply chain from commit to cluster: CI/CD runner fleets, FIPS-validated images, signed artifacts, replicated registries, private PKI
Partner with security and compliance to translate NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC controls into automated guardrails and evidence, and to triage and burn down security findings
Write clear design notes, merge request reviews, and runbooks, and help improve the shared AI-assisted workflows the team uses every day
Roll out and support AI developer tooling (Claude Code and similar) with managed settings, and review, harden, and operate the MCP servers and agent runtimes our teams depend on
Required Skills and Experience

text:

Regular

• Maintain a high state of cleanliness and utilize a clean-as-you-go process when executing maintenance duties.
• Perform regular Foreign Object Damage (FOD) walks.
• Comply with processes and procedures as per DHS/Department of Defense (DOD) documents and publications.
• Maintain control tools. Report missing, lost, found, or unattended tools to the supervisor. Inventory and inspect tools on a regular basis and replace worn or broken tools.

title: Sr. Systems Engineer
text:
Yulista Services LLC 
Regular 
Position Summary 
Yulista's Aerospace & Systems Engineering (ASE) group is seeking an experienced Senior Systems Engineer to provide technical leadership and systems engineering expertise in support of military aviation, aircraft modification, systems integration, and airworthiness certification initiatives.
The successful candidate will lead multidisciplinary engineering efforts throughout the aircraft systems lifecycle, including requirements development, system architecture, design integration, verification and validation, flight testing, and certification. This position requires a strong understanding of military aircraft systems, engineering processes, and airworthiness requirements, with the ability to translate complex technical requirements into executable engineering solutions.
The ideal candidate brings direct experience supporting military aviation programs, integrating aircraft systems and subsystems, leading technical teams, and supporting airworthiness certification activities.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities 
Lead systems engineering activities supporting military aircraft modifications, modernization, and systems integration.
Oversee the integration of aircraft systems and subsystems, including avionics, electrical, mechanical, structural, and mission equipment.
Develop, review, and manage system requirements, engineering specifications, interface documentation, and technical deliverables.
Support military aircraft airworthiness certification, compliance assessments, engineering substantiation, and approval documentation.
Lead multidisciplinary engineering teams through design, integration, verification, validation, and testing activities.
Provide technical leadership in resolving complex engineering challenges, evaluating system performance, and mitigating technical risks.
Conduct engineering design reviews, technical assessments, and configuration management activities.
Collaborate with program managers, government customers, and engineering stakeholders to ensure technical requirements, schedules, and program objectives are achieved.
Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities 
Strong knowledge of aircraft systems engineering principles and integration methodologies.
Understanding of military aircraft systems, subsystem interfaces, and aircraft modification processes.
Knowledge of airworthiness certification principles, compliance documentation, and flight safety considerations.
Ability to evaluate complex technical issues and develop practical engineering solutions.
Experience conducting engineering design reviews, technical assessments, and risk evaluations.
Strong technical writing, documentation, communication, and presentation skills.
Ability to lead cross-functional engineering teams and coordinate multiple technical priorities.
Preferred Qualifications 
Experience supporting U.S. Army aviation programs, particularly UH-60 Black Hawk , CH-47 Chinook, AH-64 Apache, or comparable military aircraft.
Experience with rotary-wing aircraft integration, modernization, or modification programs.
Familiarity with MIL-HDBK-516 , Army airworthiness processes, and Airworthiness Release (AWR) documentation.
Experience supporting FAA certification, Supplemental Type Certificates (STCs), or other aircraft certification activities.
Experience with avionics integration, mission equipment installation, aircraft electrical systems, or structural modifications.
Experience supporting ground and flight test programs, including test planning, execution, and certification support.
Experience with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), SysML, or digital engineering methodologies.
Familiarity with engineering tools such as DOORS, Cameo, MATLAB/Simulink, or comparable requirements management and modeling platforms.
Experience supporting Department of Defense aviation acquisition, sustainment, modernization, or engineering programs.
Professional Engineer (PE) license, INCOSE certification, or advanced engineering degree.
Minimum Qualifications 
Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline from an ABET-accredited program.
Minimum of 10 years of relevant engineering experience , including military aviation, aircraft systems integration, modifications, or modernization.
Demonstrated experience supporting aircraft airworthiness certification, engineering compliance, or related approval processes.
Proven technical leadership experience supporting multidisciplinary engineering teams and complex engineering projects.

title: Senior Platform Engineer
text:
StraitSys Inc 
Regular 
Primary Function 
This position has a start date in January 2027. We are accepting applications and interviewing now, and the selected candidate will begin work on or after January 4, 2027.
We are hiring a Senior Platform Engineer to design, build, and operate the delivery platform used across our enterprise IT organization. The platform is built on self-managed GitLab Ultimate and Azure managed services, including Azure Kubernetes Service, and it provides the shared CI/CD templates, security controls, and deployment automation that our containerized microservices depend on.
This is a collaborative role, and you will have significant influence over the platform's architecture as it is built out. You will work directly with developers and infrastructure engineers on how our services are built, tested, secured, and deployed. You will also define how GitLab is structured and governed, including across separate cloud environments with different compliance boundaries. Our standard is that infrastructure, pipelines, and access policy are defined as code, and that every change is reviewed through a merge request and applied by a pipeline. Part of this role is bringing the remaining manual processes to that standard.
Essential Duties 
GitLab 
Install, upgrade, patch, back up, and restore self-managed GitLab Ultimate and the RHEL servers that host it and manage the GitLab runners and identity provider integration.
Configure and administer GitLab add-ons and integrations, including GitLab Duo Enterprise.
Deploy and configure new GitLab instances when required, including in separate cloud environments, and control which code, packages, and images move between them.
Design the group and project structure of GitLab, including permissions, access tokens, and the placement of shared templates.
Build the controls that enforce the organization's security and compliance requirements on every project, including security policy projects, approval rules, compliance frameworks, and protected branches, all managed as code.
CI/CD and security 
Own the shared CI/CD template library and project templates that every service builds and deploys from, and onboard new services onto the platform.
Define and maintain container build standards, including multi-stage builds, minimal and hardened base images, non-root runtime users, and image scanning before images are pushed to the registry.
Design pipeline structure and environment promotion, including merge request and branch pipeline rules, protected environments, deployment approvals, and validation jobs that run before and after each deployment.
Integrate automated testing, code coverage, and the full GitLab Ultimate security scanning suite into the pipelines, including SAST, secret detection and push protection, dependency and license scanning, container scanning, infrastructure as code scanning, DAST, and API security testing.
Set the thresholds that block a merge or deployment, and map test and scan results to secure development controls so that the pipeline produces the audit evidence.
Introduce and operate automated dependency management across all repositories, so that library, base image, and tool updates are submitted as merge requests and tested by the pipeline before merge.
Automate versioning, release, and rollback for applications, and keep the development and pipeline toolchain current, including SDKs, build and CLI tools, CI and base images, and the supported versions of GitLab, Kubernetes, and other platform components.
Kubernetes and Azure 
Administer AKS and the other Azure managed services the workloads use, including upgrades, ingress and Gateway API, network policy, workload identity, capacity, and backup.
Define the Kubernetes deployment standards every service follows, including health probes, resource requests and limits, PodDisruptionBudgets, autoscaling, pod security context, and label and naming conventions.
Support developers in deploying and troubleshooting containerized microservices built with .NET, Node.js, and React.
Manage how configuration and secrets reach workloads and pipelines, including Key Vault integration, environment-specific configuration, protected and masked CI/CD variables, and build-time secret mounts.
Define Azure resources, including identities and cluster configuration, in Terraform, OpenTofu, or Bicep, and help infrastructure teams convert manual procedures into automated, version-controlled processes.
Automate TLS certificate issuance and renewal, define monitoring and alerting for GitLab (including its runners) and AKS, and diagnose and resolve platform failures.
Team practices 
Define the development team's source control practices (branching, merge request review, approvals), enforce them through GitLab settings, and review developer changes to pipelines, Dockerfiles, and Kubernetes manifests.
Participate in the development team's Scrum ceremonies to plan deployments, prepare environments, and coordinate releases.
Document platform architecture, standards, runbooks, and changes, and work alongside enterprise IT team members who are new to Git and to the platform tooling, including GitLab, to build their proficiency.
Supervisory Responsibilities 
This position has no supervisory responsibilities.
Desired Knowledge, Skills & Abilities 
Experience with Azure Government and with operating platforms across multiple cloud environments that have separate compliance boundaries.
Knowledge of NIST 800-171 or CMMC 2.0 controls and of STIG hardening for RHEL.
Experience implementing software supply chain controls, including SBOM generation, image signing, hardened container images, and policy as code for Kubernetes and pipelines.
Experience designing reusable infrastructure as code modules in Terraform, OpenTofu, or Bicep, including remote state management, drift detection, and plan and apply workflows that run through CI/CD pipelines with merge request review.
Experience with Helm chart development, Kustomize overlays, and GitOps delivery.
Experience with the Kubernetes Gateway API using Traefik or another implementation.
Experience with automated dependency update tools such as Renovate or Dependabot.
Experience managing Linux server configuration as code with a tool such as Ansible, Puppet, or Chef.
Experience automating certificate management with ACME.
Experience with Entra ID application registrations and with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC for APIs and single-page applications.
Experience enforcing security and compliance requirements in GitLab with security policies and compliance frameworks.
Experience administering Gitlab Self-Managed and GitLab Duo Enterprise.
Proficiency in PowerShell for Windows automation, with the ability to write maintainable, tested scripts.
Certifications such as CKA, CKS, RHCSA, RHCE, CompTIA Security+, or GitLab, Terraform, or Azure certifications.
Required Qualifications 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
7 or more years in DevOps, platform engineering, or infrastructure engineering.
Hands-on GitLab CI/CD experience, including reusable templates that multiple projects consume (for example include, extends, rules, and needs).
Administration of a self-managed GitLab instance, including new installations, upgrades, backup and restore, runners, and permissions.
5 or more years administering production Linux servers as the primary focus of your systems work, preferably RHEL, including systemd, SELinux, storage, and package management.
Experience integrating automated tests, code coverage reporting, and security scanning into CI/CD pipelines, and tracking findings through remediation with developers.
Production Kubernetes experience, preferably AKS, including deploying and troubleshooting containerized microservices, health probes, resource requests and limits, RBAC, and cluster networking and DNS.
Experience writing and optimizing

Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Experience with use of inspection gages and measuring equipment.

text:
Worker Type 
Regular 
Job Description 
AV is looking for a highly talented detail-driven Production Engineer to support the Missile Defense Agency Targets and Countermeasures team (MDA/DTTS).  In this role, you will be directly responsible for verifying that critical missile flight hardware and propulsion systems are designed, fabricated, integrated, and tested strictly in accordance with baseline standards.  You will evaluate prime contractor design and manufacturing processes, conduct technical reviews, and enforce compliance with industry mission assurance frameworks --specifically AIAA S-113 (Criteria for Explosive Systems and Devices on Space and Launch Vehicles) and related aerospace standards (such as AIAA S-114, AIAA S-080/081, SMC-S-016, or AFSPCMAN 91-710).
Design & Build Verification: Audit prime contractor engineering designs, drawing packages, manufacturing processes, and assembly records to ensure end items are built strictly to approved baseline specifications and flight-worthiness requirements.
AIAA S-113 & Standards Compliance: Apply AIAA S-113 (and related space/launch vehicle standards) to assess ordnance, explosive devices, pyrotechnic separation mechanisms, pressure vessels, and mechanical/propulsion subsystems across all design and production phases.
Peer Reviews & Milestone Gates: Participate in technical baseline reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, MRR, FRR), ensuring objective evidence supports mission assurance criteria before moving to integration and flight test.

Position Summary 
AV is seeking a Senior Program Director to lead the Next Generation C-UAS Missile (NGCM) program and advance the Freedom Eagle-1 (FE-1) missile system from development and demonstration through qualification, operational deployment and production.
The Senior Program Director will serve as the accountable program leader, owning cost, schedule, technical performance, contractual delivery and financial results. This leader will direct an integrated team across engineering, test, manufacturing, quality, supply chain and business functions.
The position requires demonstrated program-level Earned Value Management System (EVMS) leadership and a proven record of transitioning complex defense hardware from prototype development into production. Successful candidates will demonstrate direct ownership of program decisions and measurable execution results.
Key Responsibilities 
Program Execution and Financial Accountability 
Own overall program execution, profit and loss, financial forecasts and delivery of contractual commitments. 
Establish and execute an integrated program plan connecting development, qualification, flight testing, customer integration, manufacturing readiness and production. 
Direct program priorities, resource allocation and recovery actions across functional organizations. 
Establish clear accountability for program milestones, deliverables and performance outcomes. 
Lead program reviews with executive leadership and the government customer, presenting accurate performance assessments, decisions required and corrective actions. 
EVMS and Integrated Program Controls 
Own the integrated program baseline and ensure alignment among technical scope, schedule, budget and authorized work. 
Lead baseline development and maintenance, including the Work Breakdown Structure, Integrated Master Schedule, control account structure and Performance Measurement Baseline. 
Direct Control Account Managers and partner with Program Finance and Planning to maintain objective performance measurement and credible forecasts. 
Lead program-level Estimate at Completion reviews and approve forecast assumptions, corrective actions and recovery plans within delegated authority. 
Evaluate cost and schedule variances, critical-path changes, supplier performance and risks to program commitments. 
Maintain disciplined baseline change control and ensure authorized changes are incorporated into execution plans. 
Lead program participation in Integrated Baseline Reviews and applicable EVMS reviews or surveillance. 
Transition from Prototype to Production 
Own the integrated transition plan from development hardware to a qualified, configuration-controlled and producible missile system. 
Establish measurable readiness criteria for production entry and subsequent increases in production rate. 
Integrate design maturity, qualification results, manufacturing processes, supplier capacity, tooling, facilities, workforce and material availability into the transition plan. 
Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality to resolve producibility issues and translate approved designs into repeatable manufacturing processes. 
Align facility investments, capital equipment and long-lead procurement with program milestones and production demand. 
Lead production readiness reviews and ensure identified gaps have accountable owners and executable closure plans. 
Drive improvements in yield, cycle time, unit cost, quality and delivery performance as production matures. 
Supplier and Subcontractor Performance 
Hold major subcontractors accountable for technical performance, quality, cost, schedule and delivery. 
Integrate supplier commitments and risks into the program baseline and financial forecast. 
Lead supplier performance reviews, recovery plans and executive escalations. 
Partner with Contracts and Subcontracts to establish clear scope, acceptance criteria, reporting requirements and change-control processes. 
Customer and Organizational Leadership 
Serve as the principal program interface with the government customer and key industry partners. 
Lead a multidisciplinary team of direct and matrixed personnel, resolving competing priorities and securing functional commitments. 
Maintain an active risk and opportunity process with funded mitigation plans, accountable owners and timely decisions. 
Lead program planning for follow-on development and production awards, including proposals, estimates and negotiations. 
Build a culture of ownership, transparent reporting and disciplined execution.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, finance or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 
At least 15 years of progressively responsible experience in defense or aerospace, including leadership of complex defense hardware programs. 
Demonstrated experience as the accountable Program Manager or Program Director for a major defense hardware program, with ownership of financial performance, contractual delivery, technical execution and customer commitments. 
Demonstrated program-level EVMS leadership, including responsibility for baseline establishment, integrated cost and schedule performance, Estimate at Completion development, corrective action and baseline change control. Experience must extend beyond individual control account management to overall program performance. 
Demonstrated success leading a defense hardware product from development or prototype testing into initial production, including responsibility for manufacturing readiness, supplier readiness, configuration control and production delivery. 
Experience owning program budgets, financial forecasts, resource allocation and execution recovery plans. 
Experience directing integrated engineering, test, manufacturing, quality, supply chain and business teams. 
Experience managing major subcontractors and resolving significant supplier technical, quality, cost or schedule issues. 
Working knowledge of EIA-748 EVMS principles, integrated scheduling, critical-path management and risk management. 
Experience serving as a principal program representative to government customers and executive leadership. 
Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearance required for the position. 
Ability to travel to customer, supplier, manufacturing and test locations as program needs require. 
Candidates must demonstrate accountable ownership and measurable results in the required areas. Experience supporting program reviews, coordinating activities, tracking schedules or preparing reports is relevant but does not, by itself, satisfy the program leadership requirements.

Experience leading missile, interceptor, guided weapon, air defense or counter-UAS programs. 
Experience supporting U.S. Army acquisition programs and government program offices. 
Experience leading qualification activities, flight-test campaigns, production readiness reviews and low-rate initial production. 
Experience establishing or expanding manufacturing facilities and production capacity. 
Experience with customer EVMS surveillance and Integrated Baseline Reviews. 
Familiarity with Manufacturing Readiness Levels and Technology Readiness Levels. 
Experience managing development and production across multiple contract types. 
Advanced degree in engineering, business administration or a related discipline. 
Project Management Professional certification.

A credible program baseline that integrates technical scope, schedule, resources and financial commitments. 
Accurate forecasts and timely corrective action supported by objective performance data.

title: Cybersecurity Engineer - Incident Response
text:
Worker Type 
Regular 
Job Description 
Summary 
The Cybersecurity Engineer investigates and responds to cybersecurity incidents while engineering improvements to the organization's incident response capabilities. This role combines hands-on technical investigation with the development of detections, response workflows, and security platform configurations that help the organization identify, contain, and recover from threats.
The ideal candidate has a strong background in Microsoft security technologies, experience supporting security operations, and the ability to turn lessons learned from incidents into measurable improvements. This position requires sound technical judgment, clear communication, and close collaboration with security analysts, IT teams, and business stakeholders.
Position Responsibilities 
Investigate and respond to security incidents involving endpoints, identities, email, cloud services, and enterprise infrastructure.
Perform incident scoping, timeline reconstruction, root cause analysis, and impact assessments using available telemetry and forensic evidence.
Coordinate containment, eradication, and recovery activities with system owners while minimizing business disruption.
Use Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, and Microsoft Entra ID to investigate threats and support response actions.
Develop and tune Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries, analytics rules, detections, and hunting queries to improve threat visibility and reduce false positives.
Improve security logging, data collection, and platform integrations to address gaps identified during investigations.
Develop and maintain incident response plans, playbooks, runbooks, escalation procedures, and incident classification criteria.
Lead or support post-incident reviews, document lessons learned, and track corrective actions through completion.
Identify recurring incident patterns and implement engineering changes that address underlying weaknesses.
Partner with automation engineers to streamline alert enrichment, evidence collection, case management, and approved containment actions.
Produce clear incident reports that document findings, business impact, response actions, and recommended improvements.
Conduct tabletop exercises and technical response drills to validate procedures and strengthen team readiness.
Preserve investigation evidence and maintain accurate records in accordance with organizational requirements.
Measure incident response effectiveness through detection and containment times, repeat incidents, playbook coverage, and corrective action completion.
Support incident response coverage, including participation in an established on-call rotation as required.
Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Experience) 
Three or more years of experience in cybersecurity engineering, incident response, security operations, or a related technical role.
Hands-on experience investigating and responding to incidents in Microsoft-based enterprise environments.
Experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, and Microsoft Defender XDR.
Proficiency with KQL for log analysis, threat hunting, and detection development.
Working knowledge of Windows security, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, and Azure.
Understanding of incident response frameworks and the ability to apply structured investigation, containment, eradication, and recovery practices.
Experience analyzing endpoint, identity, email, and network telemetry to identify malicious activity and determine incident scope.

title: Capture Manager
text:
Who We Are 
Griffon Aerospace designs, builds, and flies unmanned aerial systems that perform. We are a focused team of engineers and operators who care about mission success before satisfying any other "metrics." We don't hand work off and walk away. We own it. Our culture is defined by technical rigor, follow-through, and refusal to accept "good enough." 
The Role 
We're looking for a Capture Manager who has demonstrated success in identifying and winning Department of War contract opportunities that align with our business products and objectives. You'll work directly under our VP of Programs and lead the capture process for Griffon's proposals and growth opportunities. The Capture Manager will find, qualify, and build response strategies on open or soon to release bid opportunities. You will lead the proposal team consisting of engineering, business, and corporate stakeholders through the proposal writing process with a clear but agile plan. You will not just create the plan; however, you must also own the execution and be an authoring SME in the response documents. 
You should know your way around the Department of War acquisition process, understand what it takes to shape a compliant response and build a teaming strategy before an RFP ever drops. You should have a demonstrated history of running color team reviews and briefing a program executive office. 
Key Responsibilities 
Own the Capture 
– Qualify and prioritize opportunities against Griffon's strategy, resources, and realistic probability of winning. 
– Build and drive the capture plan that covers customer engagement, competitive assessment, teaming strategy, and win themes. 
– Own the black hat/competitive analysis and shape win strategy around Griffon's real technical and past-performance discriminators. 
– Brief capture status, gate reviews, and bid/no-bid recommendations to leadership with a clear-eyed view of probability of winning. 
Lead the Proposal 
– Lead proposal development end-to-end: outline, compliance matrix, writing assignments, and schedule, holding the team to the RFP requirements and the win strategy. 
– Write and edit proposal content yourself where it matters most: executive summaries, technical volumes, and past performance. We are not looking for a spreadsheet manager. 
– Run color team reviews (pink, red, gold) and drive substantive rewrites based on findings, not just cosmetic edits. 
– Coordinate pricing, contracts, and teaming inputs into a single, compliant, compelling proposal delivered on time. 
Build the Pipeline 
– Develop and maintain relationships with government program offices, primes, and teammates relevant to Griffon's target markets. 
– Represent Griffon at industry days, conferences, and customer engagements, translating what you hear into actionable capture activity. 
– Partner with engineering and corporate leadership ahead of RFP release. 
Report to the VP of Programs 
– Provide direct visibility into capture status and proposal outcomes to the VP of Programs and executive leadership. 
– Track win/loss results and drive lessons-learned back into the capture process so Griffon gets better at this every cycle. 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
– Bachelor's degree; relevant capture or proposal certifications (e.g., APMP, Shipley) are a plus, but your track record matters more. 
– 7+ years in defense capture management or business development, with a demonstrated history of writing and leading winning proposal efforts within the Department of War acquisition system. 
– Direct experience running the full capture lifecycle: opportunity qualification, black hat sessions, teaming, proposal development, and color team reviews. 
– Working knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Department of War source selection processes. 
– Strong writing skills. Demonstrate that you can produce compelling proposal content yourself, not just manage people who do. 
– U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. 
Strongly Preferred 
– Active security clearance. 
– Established relationships within relevant program executive offices (e.g., PEO Aviation, Missiles & Space, AvMC, SOCOM) or primes in the UAS market. 
– Experience capturing and winning UAS, launched effects, or precision-guided munitions programs. 
– APMP or Shipley capture/proposal management certification. 
The Kind of Person Who Thrives Here 
You show up. 
When something is broken in the field, you're on a plane. You don't manage from behind a screen. 
You don't quit. 
Problems are resolved, not deferred. You find a way or you make one. 
You own the outcome but share the glory. 
The whole thing. If the program is late, that's yours. If it delivers, the team is praised not just you. 
You communicate first. 
Plans, issues, and new data travel fast here. 
What Griffon Offers 
Competitive salary commensurate with experience and clearance level 
Comprehensive benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match 
Paid time off and 10 federal holidays 
Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates 
A small company where your decisions matter and your fingerprints are on real hardware flying real missions 
Griffon Aerospace – Come Build the Unfair Advantage.

title: Flight Control & Avionics Hardware – Responsible Engineer
text:
Who We Are 
Griffon Aerospace designs, builds, and flies unmanned aerial systems that perform. We are a focused team of engineers and operators who care about mission success before satisfying any other "metrics." We don't hand work off and walk away. We own it. Our culture is defined by technical rigor, follow-through, and refusal to accept "good enough." 
The Role 
We're looking for someone to take ownership of our custom flight control hardware and avionics components across our UAS portfolio. Griffon hires engineers who have built things that fly and know what it means to carry a board from schematic to flight line. You'll own the spiral development lifecycle of our flight control hardware end-to-end. 
You should know your way around an aircraft development program, understand what integration with flight software and airframes involves, and be comfortable working at a test bench or the flight line as easily as at a desk running analysis tools. 
This role is responsible for ensuring flight control hardware reliability and airworthiness from concept through fielded sustainment, including new hardware development, sustaining engineering on deployed platforms, supplier oversight, and certification support. The ideal candidate combines hands-on avionics hardware expertise with the systems-engineering discipline needed to manage a critical subsystem through iterative spiral development and its full lifecycle. 
Key Responsibilities 
Design & Spiral Development Engineering 
– Lead design, analysis, and iterative spiral development of custom flight control hardware and the avionics stack, including processing, sensor, power, and interface subsystems. 
– Own root-cause investigations and corrective actions for hardware issues identified in test or in the field; manage engineering change requests through the full approval cycle across each development spiral. 
– Balance size, weight, power (SWaP), redundancy, and reliability trade-offs specific to UAV flight control requirements. 
– Collaborate with firmware, software, airframe, and manufacturing teams to ensure flight control hardware and avionics integration meets platform-level requirements. 
– Provide technical support to production, field service, and customer support teams for fielded avionics hardware. 
Reliability & Durability Testing 
– Develop and execute test plans for environmental, EMI/EMC, vibration, and thermal qualification of flight control hardware and avionics. 
– Define and track reliability metrics (MTBF, MTBUR) and failure modes across fielded avionics hardware; drive design and process changes from test and field data. 
– Oversee bench and flight test instrumentation, data collection, and reporting for avionics and flight control test campaigns. 
– Maintain engineering documentation, schematics, BOMs, and interface control documents in compliance with applicable military and industry standards. 
– Prepare technical substantiation, test reports, and compliance evidence for customer and regulatory review. 
Supplier & Vendor Management 
– Identify, qualify, and manage suppliers of avionics components, custom PCBs, and flight control hardware, including source inspections and incoming quality requirements. 
– Manage supplier corrective action requests (SCARs) and work with vendors to resolve quality, cost, and schedule issues. 
– Support make/buy decisions and second-source strategies to reduce supply chain risk for critical flight control and avionics components. 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
– Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field. 
– 7+ years of experience in electrical/avionics hardware design, development, or sustaining engineering, with direct hands-on experience in flight control or embedded avionics hardware. 
– Demonstrated experience taking hardware through a qualification or certification process. 
– Experience managing suppliers or vendors for custom PCBs or critical electronic components. 
– Working knowledge of reliability engineering principles (FMEA, root-cause analysis, MTBF/MTBUR). 
– Proficiency with EDA/schematic capture tools (e.g., Altium, OrCAD, or equivalent) and engineering documentation/PLM systems. 
– Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing technical reports and customer-facing documentation. 
– U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. 
Strongly Preferred 
– Experience with UAV/UAS flight control systems, autopilots, or other small, high-reliability embedded avionics. 
– Familiarity with military airworthiness or certification standards (e.g., MIL-HDBK-516, DO-254, DO-160, AS9100 quality systems). 
– Experience with avionics test bench design, instrumentation, and data acquisition systems. 
– Background supporting DoD or government aerospace programs. 
– Master's degree in a relevant engineering discipline. 
The Kind of Person Who Thrives Here 
You show up. 
When something is broken in the field, you're on a plane. You don't manage from behind a screen. 
You don't quit. 
Problems are resolved, not deferred. You find a way or you make one. 
You own the outcome but share the glory. 
The whole thing. If the program is late, that's yours. If it delivers, the team is praised not just you. 
You communicate first. 
Plans, issues, and new data travel fast here. 
What Griffon Offers 
Competitive salary commensurate with experience and clearance level 
Comprehensive benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match 
Paid time off and 10 federal holidays 
Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates 
A small company where your decisions matter and your fingerprints are on real hardware flying real missions 
Griffon Aerospace – Come Build the Unfair Advantage.

title: Program Manager, Valiant UAS
text:
Who We Are 
Griffon Aerospace designs, builds, and flies unmanned aerial systems that perform. We are a small, focused team of engineers and operators who care firstly about mission success before satisfying any other "metrics." We don't hand work off and walk away. We own it. Our culture is defined by technical rigor, relentless follow-through, and a refusal to accept "good enough" when our customers' missions are on the line. 
The Valiant UAS program is one of our premier product lines, and we need a Program Manager who treats it that way. We need a candidate who can manage schedule, technical risk, and customer relationships in parallel. 
The Role 
As the Program Manager for the Valiant UAS portfolio, you are the single accountable leader for everything that touches this program: budget, schedule, technical performance, customer satisfaction, and team execution. You are not a coordinator or a facilitator. You are the owner. 
This is a hands-on role. You will be on the flight line when things are getting sorted out. You will be in the lab when the engineering teams need to make critical decisions. You will be on the phone when a customer faces challenges, and you will already have a recovery plan ready to make them whole and confident in our commitments to their success. You will lead cross-functional teams of engineers, technicians, and support staff, and you will set the standard for what ownership looks like every single day. 
What You'll Own 
Program Execution 
Full concept-to-lifecycle responsibility for the Valiant UAS portfolio across all active contracts and development efforts 
Develop, maintain, and actively manage integrated master schedules (IMS) with real milestones to minimize dependence on purely success-based goals 
Drive cost, schedule, and technical performance to plan; identify and burn down risk before they can be realized 
Lead monthly program reviews, CDRs, PDRs, and customer milestone events 
Own the financial baseline and variance analysis to mitigate surprises to leadership or the customer 
Technical Responsibility 
Facilitate technical decision making across the program; understand the system deeply enough to challenge assumptions and make informed trades 
Partner with Engineering, Flight Test, and Manufacturing to ensure technical requirements are achievable, tested, and delivered 
Facilitate rapid decision-making when design, test, or fielding issues arise 
Engage directly in failure investigations, root cause analyses, and corrective action follow-through 
Customer & Stakeholder Management 
Be the primary interface to Government program offices, prime contractors, and end users 
Communicate status, risks, and issues proactively 
Identify and capture follow-on business, contract modifications, and program growth opportunities 
Represent Griffon at industry events, customer visits, and proposal activities as required 
Team & Culture 
Build and lead a high-performing, low-ego team that runs toward problems, not away from them 
Mentor junior program staff; establish practices and standards that outlast any single program 
Embody and enforce Griffon's ownership culture: every team member knows their piece and is accountable for it 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Aerospace, Systems, or a closely related technical discipline 
7+ years of program management experience in defense aerospace, UAS, or adjacent fields 
Demonstrated track record managing DoD development or production programs from $5M to $50M+ 
Hands-on experience with aircraft or UAS systems 
Strong command of program management fundamentals: EVM, IMS, risk management, CDR/PDR processes 
Active Secret clearance (or ability to obtain) 
Comfortable traveling to customer sites, field operations, and test events up to 30% 
Strongly Preferred 
Master's degree in Engineering or Business (MBA), or equivalent operational experience 
Direct experience with Group 2–4 UAS programs in development, test, or production 
Familiarity with MIL-STD airworthiness, DO-178/DO-254, or UAS-specific certification pathways 
PMP, DAWIA, or equivalent program management certification 
Prior military aviation or UAS operational background 
Active Top-Secret clearance 
What Griffon Offers 
Competitive salary commensurate with experience and clearance level 
Comprehensive benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match 
Paid time off and 10 paid holidays 
Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates 
A small company where your decisions matter and your fingerprints are on real hardware flying real missions

title: Technical Product Manager – Group I FPV/Quadcopter Systems
text:
Who We Are 
Griffon Aerospace designs, builds, and flies unmanned aerial systems that perform. We are a focused team of engineers and operators who care about mission success before satisfying any other "metrics." We don't hand work off and walk away. We own it. Our culture is defined by technical rigor, follow-through, and refusal to accept "good enough." 
The Role 
We're looking for someone who has actually built things that fly and knows what it takes to turn a good design into hundreds of good units. You'll own Griffon's Group 1 multi-rotor product line end-to-end. Aircraft scale cleanly in production and a supply chain that can keep up with it. 
You should know your way around small UAS hardware, understand what it takes to design volume rather than one-off builds, and be comfortable on a supplier's shop floor or in an integration lab as easily as at a desk running analysis tools. 
Key Responsibilities 
Product Ownership 
– Define and own the product engineering for Griffon's Group 1 FPV/quadcopter systems. 
– Drive requirements, design priorities, and performance envelopes across airframe, propulsion, power, and RF/video link 
– Write SRDs and ICDs that engineers, suppliers, and integration partners can build to, not just check a box with. 
– Run trade studies on platform configurations, component commonality, and design-for-cost across product variants. 
Design for Scale 
– Lead design decisions that trade one-off performance for producibility, driving toward designs that scale cleanly from tens to hundreds of units without a redesign. 
– Standardize components and subassemblies across quadcopter variants to simplify production, sparing, and field support. 
– Partner with manufacturing engineering to move designs into low-rate and full-rate production at the right unit cost and delivery rate. 
Build a Supply Chain That Scales 
– Identify, qualify, and manage suppliers for airframes, motors, ESCs, batteries, and RF components, with an eye toward lead time, single points of failure, and cost at volume. 
– Build second source and multi-source strategies for critical components to keep production moving through shortages or supplier issues. 
– Manage supplier corrective action requests (SCARs) and hold vendors accountable for quality, cost, and schedule. 
Lead Integration with Autonomy and Payload Partners 
– Serve as the primary technical interface with external autonomy and payload providers, translating their interface requirements into something Griffon's engineering team can work with. 
– Manage the interface control process across autonomy stacks, payload bays, and Griffon's airframe and electrical systems, keeping every partner aligned as designs evolve. 
– Get hands-on integration testing - bench and flight - to find and fix interface issues before they hit the field. 
– Track and communicate program status, risk, and technical performance to leadership and customers - no sugarcoating. 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
– Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, or Systems Engineering. 
– 5+ years in UAS or small unmanned systems product development, with direct experience taking a design from prototype to production. 
– Demonstrated experience managing a multi-vendor supply chain for hardware at volume. 
– Experience integrating third-party autonomy or payload systems into a fielded platform. 
– Working knowledge of design-for-manufacturability (DFM) and design-for-cost (DFC) principles. 
– Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience writing requirements and interface documentation. 
– U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. 
Strongly Preferred 
– Experience with Group 1 UAS, FPV platforms, or small quadcopter/multirotor systems. 
– Background working with commercial or DoD autonomy stacks (e.g., PX4, ArduPilot, or proprietary). 
– Experience taking small UAS hardware through low-rate and full-rate production ramp. 
– Background supporting DoD or government aerospace programs. 
– Master's degree in relevant engineering discipline. 
The Kind of Person Who Thrives Here 
You show up. 
When something is broken in the field, you're on a plane. You don't manage from behind a screen. 
You don't quit. 
Problems are resolved, not deferred. You find a way or you make one. 
You own the outcome but share the glory. 
The whole thing. If the program is late, that's yours. If it delivers, the team is praised not just you. 
You communicate first. 
Plans, issues, and new data travel fast here. 
What Griffon Offers 
Competitive salary commensurate with experience and clearance level 
Comprehensive benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match 
Paid time off and 10 federal holidays 
Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates 
A small company where your decisions matter and your fingerprints are on real hardware flying real missions

title: UAS Combustion Engine Systems
text:
Who We Are 
Griffon Aerospace designs, builds, and flies unmanned aerial systems that perform. We are a focused team of engineers and operators who care about mission success before satisfying any other "metrics." We don't hand work off and walk away. We own it. Our culture is defined by technical rigor, follow-through, and refusal to accept "good enough." 
The Role 
We're looking for someone to take ownership of our internal combustion systems across our UAS portfolio. Griffon both works with suppliers and develops our own propulsion systems. Small two-stroke engine specialty is required. Griffon hires engineers who have built things that fly and know what it means to get hardware from a drawing board to a flight line. You'll own the lifecycle of up to 4 different engine platforms end-to-end - from the first requirement written to the last configuration signed off before production - and you'll be in the weeds with every engineering team and contractor that touches it along the way. 
You should know your way around an aircraft development program, understand what integration involves, and be comfortable working at a test range or a factory floor as easily as at a desk running analysis tools. 
This role is responsible for ensuring engine reliability and airworthiness from concept through fielded sustainment, including new engine development, sustaining engineering on deployed platforms, supplier oversight, and certification support. The ideal candidate combines hands-on two-stroke engine expertise with the systems-engineering discipline needed to manage a critical component through its full lifecycle. 
Key Responsibilities 
Design & Sustaining Engineering 
– Lead design, analysis, and continuous improvement of two-stroke UAV engines, including fuel systems, ignition, cooling, and induction/exhaust tuning. 
– Own root-cause investigations and corrective actions for engine issues identified in test or in the field; manage engineering change requests through the full approval cycle. 
– Balance power density, fuel efficiency, weight, and reliability trade-offs specific to UAV operating envelopes and mission profiles. 
– Collaborate with airframe, avionics, and manufacturing teams to ensure engine integration meets platform-level requirements. 
– Provide technical support to production, field service, and customer support teams for fielded engines. 
Reliability & Durability Testing 
– Develop and execute test plans for endurance, environmental, and altitude/thermal qualification of engines and components. 
– Define and track reliability metrics (MTBF, MTBUR) and failure modes across the engine fleet; drive design and process changes from test and field data. 
– Oversee bench and flight test instrumentation, data collection, and reporting for propulsion test campaigns. 
– Maintain engineering documentation, drawings, and technical data packages in compliance with applicable military and industry standards. 
– Prepare technical substantiation, test reports, and compliance evidence for customer and regulatory review. 
Supplier & Vendor Management 
– Identify, qualify, and manage engine and component suppliers, including source inspections and incoming quality requirements. 
– Manage supplier corrective action requests (SCARs) and work with vendors to resolve quality, cost, and schedule issues. 
– Support make/buy decisions and second-source strategies to reduce supply chain risk for critical engine components. 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
– Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. 
– 7+ years of experience in internal combustion engine design, development, or sustaining engineering, with direct hands-on experience with two-stroke engines. 
– Demonstrated experience taking an engine or engine component through a qualification or certification process. 
– Experience managing suppliers or vendors for critical mechanical components. 
– Working knowledge of reliability engineering principles (FMEA, root-cause analysis, MTBF/MTBUR). 
– Proficiency with CAD tools (e.g., SolidWorks or equivalent) and engineering documentation/PLM systems. 
– Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing technical reports and customer-facing documentation. 
– U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. 
Strongly Preferred 
– Experience with UAV/UAS propulsion systems or other small, high-cycle, weight-constrained engine applications. 
– Familiarity with military airworthiness or certification standards (e.g., MIL-HDBK-516, AS9100 quality systems). 
– Experience with engine test cell design, instrumentation, and data acquisition systems. 
– Background supporting DoD or government aerospace programs. 
– Master's degree in a relevant engineering discipline. 
The Kind of Person Who Thrives Here 
You show up. 
When something is broken in the field, you're on a plane. You don't manage from behind a screen. 
You don't quit. 
Problems are resolved, not deferred. You find a way or you make one. 
You own the outcome but share the glory. 
The whole thing. If the program is late, that's yours. If it delivers, the team is praised not just you. 
You communicate first. 
Plans, issues, and new data travels fast here. 
What Griffon Offers 
Competitive salary commensurate with experience and clearance level 
Comprehensive benefits: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match 
Paid time off and 11 federal holidays 
Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates 
A small company where your decisions matter and your fingerprints are on real hardware flying real missions 
Griffon Aerospace – Come Build the Unfair Advantage.

title: Configuration Administrator Senior - 3893
text:
RGNext employees execute and report on theater and strategic offensive and defensive ballistic missile testing and support space situational awareness operations and experiments, using a wide array of highly sophisticated radar, telemetry and optical sensors to meet the needs of our nation in defending the United States and its interests.  
This position is located at the Reagan Test Range (RTR) Operations Center in Huntsville, Alabama. 
What You Will Do: 
Direct configuration and change management workflows and activities for proposed hardware and software changes, ensuring strict version control, secure documentation, and the continuous improvement of CM processes across all active baselines.
Manage and disseminate Change Request (CR) packages, hosting and participating in Technical Review Board (TRB) meetings while leveraging modern tooling and streamlined methodologies to accelerate technical evaluation and approval actions.
Conduct deep research and development to identify potential threats and vulnerabilities associated with proposed hardware and/or software changes to the enclaves, including the comprehensive onboarding and evaluation of new hardware and software.
Conduct rigorous risk assessments (RAs) for proposed changes to identify vulnerabilities and determine risk level to the target enclave prior to implementation. Produce RA reports and submit for RTR customer review and go/no go decision via CCB.
Ensure end-to-end Risk Management Framework (RMF) and system security compliance across all networks and enclaves under purview.
Prepare, review, and maintain program deliverables and status updates to clearly communicate baseline modifications and security impacts.
Champion strict adherence to change control processes while driving innovation, embedding continuous sustainment, and pioneering best practices in configuration and risk management.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications You Must Have: 
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, IT or related field, or experience in lieu of education.
Five (5) or more years experience in Industrial Security documentation with a cybersecurity focus, spanning classified and unclassified environments.
Active cybersecurity certification (e.g., Security+, CISSP, CISM, or DoD 8140 compliant).
Working knowledge of IT hardware and software components within an enterprise enclave.
Experience reviewing hardware/software STIGs and generating security policies, procedures, and reports compliant with RMF, AR 25-1, AR 25-2, and DoD/DoW regulations.
Proficient in standard productivity tools (MS Office, SharePoint, Teams) and familiar with DevSecOps, ITSM, and SIEM platforms (e.g., Jira, GitLab, ServiceDesk, ACAS).
Hands-on experience conducting deep technical research on security specs to support risk assessments, change pipelines, and configuration management.
Skilled in leveraging automation, scripting, and software tools to streamline change management lifecycles and workflows.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to explain complex security and IT issues to technical and non-technical audiences.
Self-motivated with strong organizational, time-management, and problem-solving skills under minimal supervision.
Ability to perform light physical tasks both standing/bending and ability to lift/carry/push/pull up to 25 lbs. independently.
The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued Secret security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance
Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Passport for travel to Kwajalein Atoll, if needed.
The flexibility to work occasional non-duty hours or on weekends to support specific project or mission requirements.
Benefits of Working at RGNext: 
Employees enjoy a robust benefit package on day one, which includes medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurances, generous Paid Time Off and holiday pay, a retirement savings plan with a company match and vesting on day one!  
Note: This job description describes the general nature of the duties and requirements of the job. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list or to limit the supervisor's ability to modify work assignments as appropriate.

title: Senior Systems Security Engineer
text:
nou Systems, Inc. (nSI) is a 100% ESOP company! We value teamwork and collaboration, and this transition allows us to take that commitment to a new level. nSI empowers our customers by supplying products, services, and expertise with powerful, data driven insights that transform defense systems and improve capabilities. 
nou Systems, Inc. (nSI) is seeking a Senior Systems Security Engineer to lead the integration of security into the engineering of complex mission systems. Applying the principles and practices of systems security engineering, the engineer will translate customer protection needs into requirements, shape system architectures and designs, and develop evidence that supports confidence in system security.
The successful candidate will work with systems, hardware, software, test, safety, and program teams throughout the system life cycle, from concept development and acquisition through operation, sustainment, and disposal. This senior technical role requires independent engineering judgment, hands-on development and review of technical artifacts, and the ability to explain security tradeoffs and residual risk to customers and program leadership.
Responsibilities :  
• Lead stakeholder discussions to define mission context, assets, loss concerns, protection priorities, operational environments, and measurable security objectives.
• Develop and analyze stakeholder and system security requirements; allocate requirements to system elements and interfaces; and maintain traceability to protection needs, design decisions, and verification evidence.
• Develop and evaluate security architectures and designs across hardware, software, networks, physical elements, and human interactions, including system boundaries, trust relationships, and external dependencies.
• Apply secure design principles such as least privilege, isolation, least functionality, and protective failure; document the rationale for selected mechanisms and the assumptions on which protection depends.
• Perform threat, vulnerability, and system security analyses to identify paths to unacceptable loss, including malicious activity, errors, faults, and misuse. Recommend mitigations and characterize remaining uncertainty.
• Conduct engineering trade studies that balance protection and assurance needs with mission performance, safety, reliability, cost, schedule, and life cycle constraints.
• Guide implementation and integration of security requirements; review technical specifications and supplier deliverables; and assess whether composed system elements preserve required security properties.
• Develop security verification and validation strategies, acceptance criteria, and test procedures. Evaluate whether implementation satisfies requirements and whether the delivered system meets stakeholder protection needs in its intended environment.
• Develop and maintain security assurance cases that link explicit claims, structured arguments, assumptions, and credible evidence. Identify evidence gaps and communicate their effect on confidence and risk.
• Integrate security activities into engineering plans, technical reviews, configuration management, and change control. Assess the security effects of design changes, upgrades, supplier substitutions, and sustainment actions.
• Support secure transition, operation, maintenance, and disposal, including protection of sensitive assets. Provide engineering evidence for customer acceptance and authorization decisions, and mentor engineers in repeatable SSE practices.
• Establish reusable SSE artifacts and review practices and help engineering teams apply them to active program work.
Basic Qualifications: 
• Substantial experience in systems security engineering or security architecture for complex systems, including responsibility for requirements, design decisions, technical reviews, and evaluation activities.
• Ability to apply NIST SP 800-160 Volume 1 principles and System Security Engineering (SSE) life cycle processes within a multidisciplinary systems engineering effort.
• Experience developing verifiable requirements, architecture descriptions, interface specifications, engineering analyses, and traceability records.
• Practical understanding of trust boundaries, security mechanisms, threat and vulnerability analysis, and the interactions among hardware, software, network, physical, and human system elements.
• Experience planning or conducting security verification and validation, assessing test and analysis results, and developing reasoned conclusions from technical evidence.
• Ability to lead technical work independently, resolve competing engineering priorities, mentor colleagues, and communicate tradeoffs and residual risk to technical and executive audiences.
• A degree in systems engineering, electrical or computer engineering, computer science, cybersecurity, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
• Must complete applicable nSI pre-employment checks and employment eligibility verification.
• Must be able to obtain and maintain any security clearance or customer access required for the assigned program.
• Must follow applicable customer security policies, technical data handling requirements, and program procedures.
• May travel to customer or nSI locations as required by the assignment.
Preferred Qualifications: 
Experience supporting DoD or other Federal missions.
Experience with Embedded or Cyber-Physical systems.
Experience using Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and Requirements Management tools.
Experience developing security assurance cases and familiarity with ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288.
Experience connecting SSE artifacts to Risk Management Framework and Program Protection activities.
Relevant systems engineering or security engineering certifications.

text:

We value teamwork and collaboration, and this transition allows us to take that commitment to a new level. nSI empowers our customers by supplying products, services, and expertise with powerful, data driven insights that transform defense systems and improve capabilities.
We are pleased to announce the opening for a Data Platforms Integrator (Engineer 4 / Analyst 4), who will support the Missile Defense Agency's (MDA) Next Generation Environment (NGE) program and become part of our technology company operating in missile defense, cybersecurity, test range modernization, biotechnology, and space control marketspaces. You will be part of a team known for delivering innovative technical solutions that support critical national security missions.
In this role, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor in a Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) capacity, directly supporting the Government Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and NGE leadership. You will provide technical oversight and integration guidance for the NGE Data Design Area, supporting the development of a secure, resilient hybrid multi-cloud environment.
You will evaluate existing applications, databases, and modern data platforms across AWS, Azure, and on-premises environments to ensure alignment with the Department of Defense (DoD) Zero Trust Strategy. Your work will focus on data discovery, classification, protection, and access governance to ensure mission-critical information remains secure and accessible only to authorized users.
Responsibilities: 
You'll be responsible for:
Serving as a senior technical authority in Architecture Review Boards (ARBs), evaluating proposed database architectures, data storage solutions, and data pipelines against NGE requirements and DoD Zero Trust mandates.
Conducting technical assessments of existing mission applications, relational databases, NoSQL environments, and object storage repositories to identify modernization opportunities and Zero Trust integration gaps.
Providing architectural oversight for enterprise data discovery, automated cataloging, classification, labeling, and tagging across hybrid multi-cloud environments.
Designing and validating data protection solutions, including data-at-rest encryption, automated Data Loss Prevention (DLP), data rights management, and dynamic data masking.
Ensuring data platform architectures align with DISA Thunderdome Zero Trust capabilities, including Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), and enterprise DLP policies.
Developing and evaluating fine-grained Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) solutions using Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) attributes and contextual risk assessments.
Overseeing integration of Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs) and Policy Decision Points (PDPs) to support dynamic authorization and secure data access.
Providing technical guidance for data virtualization, database security, and access governance across AWS, Azure, and on-premises VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) environments.
Ensuring compliance with DoD Data-at-Rest (DAR) requirements, Key Management Service (KMS) integration standards, Hardware Security Module (HSM) requirements, and applicable JSIG and NIST SP 800-207 guidelines.
Evaluating data platform modernization strategies and integration approaches to improve interoperability, security, and enterprise data governance.
Leading technical exchange meetings (TEMs) with integration contractors, database vendors, and security technology providers to evaluate proposed solutions and resolve cross-platform integration challenges.
Translating Government leadership requirements into actionable engineering solutions while maintaining alignment with NGE architecture and DoD cybersecurity standards.
Basic Qualifications: 
You must have a Master's degree in a STEM discipline with at least 12 years of engineering or IT architectural experience, or a Bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline with at least 20 years of relevant experience. Degrees in Computer Science, Data Management, Cybersecurity, or a related technical discipline are preferred.
You must have a minimum of 6 years of experience analyzing, architecting, and integrating complex enterprise databases, including relational database management systems (RDBMS), NoSQL platforms, storage solutions, and data pipelines.
You must have demonstrated experience designing and implementing Zero Trust data protection solutions, including automated data classification, data rights management, dynamic access governance, and encryption.
You must have hands-on experience architecting and securing enterprise data storage and analytics services across both AWS and Microsoft Azure environments.
You must have experience designing, accrediting, and operating data platforms within classified DoD environments.
You must possess an active Top Secret security clearance with current SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).
You must meet DoD 8140/8570 requirements for an IAM Level III or IASAE Level II/III position.
You must possess an active (ISC)² Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification.
You must be a U.S. citizen to be eligible for this position.
